Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: NCERT: the generative cell divides mitotically to give rise to the two male gametes, so they carry the same genetic information (Statement I true). The megaspore mother cell, however, undergoes MEIOSIS to produce four megaspores; meiosis separates homologous chromosomes (and their alleles), so the four megaspores of a heterozygous plant are not all genetically identical (Statement II false). Coming from a single cell does not make the products identical when the division is meiotic.
steps: Male gametes: mitosis of one cell → identical
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Sexual Reproduction in Flowering Plants', pre-fertilisation: pollen grain; megasporogenesis
solution.final_answer: Option C: Statement I is true but Statement II is false.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: NCERT describes two developmental processes in the ovule in which nuclear divisions are not immediately followed by cell wall formation (free-nuclear divisions). These two processes are:

options.text: Development of the embryo sac from the functional megaspore, and the most common type of endosperm development
Meiosis of the megaspore mother cell, and the development of the embryo from the zygote
Development of the embryo from the zygote, and the formation of the seed coat from the integuments
Formation of the microspore tetrad, and the development of the embryo sac from the functional megaspore

solution.explanation: NCERT: the nucleus of the functional megaspore divides mitotically, and two more sequential divisions give the 8-nucleate stage; these divisions are strictly free nuclear, i.e. not followed immediately by cell wall formation. In the most common type of endosperm development, the primary endosperm nucleus undergoes successive nuclear divisions to give free nuclei; cell wall formation follows later and the endosperm becomes cellular.
steps: Embryo sac: 2 → 4 → 8 free nuclei, then walls
Endosperm (common type): free nuclei, then cellular
solution.why_others_wrong: NCERT does not describe the embryo, the seed coat or the meiosis of spore mother cells as free nuclear; the microspore tetrad forms in the anther, not in the ovule.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Sexual Reproduction in Flowering Plants', pre-fertilisation: female gametophyte; post-fertilisation: endosperm
solution.final_answer: Option A: Development of the embryo sac from the functional megaspore, and the most common type of endosperm development

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: A typical angiosperm anther (bilobed, each lobe dithecous) releases 2560 pollen grains in all, and its microsporangia contain equal numbers of pollen mother cells. If every pollen mother cell completed microsporogenesis normally and every microspore became a pollen grain, how many pollen mother cells were present in each microsporangium?

solution.concept: From pollen grains back to pollen mother cells
solution.explanation: A bilobed anther with dithecous lobes has 2 × 2 = 4 microsporangia, so each microsporangium yields 2560/4 = 640 pollen grains. Each pollen mother cell gives a tetrad of four microspores, i.e. four pollen grains, so each microsporangium had 640/4 = 160 pollen mother cells.
solution.why_others_wrong: 640 is the number of pollen grains per microsporangium (the tetrad step is skipped); 320 counts only two microsporangia per anther; 40 divides by four once too often.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Sexual Reproduction in Flowering Plants', pre-fertilisation: the stamen, microsporangium and pollen grain; microsporogenesis
solution.final_answer: Option B: 160

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: NCERT represents the gametes of a Tt pea plant as carrying T or t, each with a chance of 1/2. The genotypes of the F2 (Tt × Tt) are then obtained from the binomial expression:

solution.concept: Binomial representation of a monohybrid cross
solution.explanation: NCERT: the gametes of a Tt plant carry T or t with equal (1/2) chance. Random fusion of gametes is shown by (1/2 T + 1/2 t)(1/2 T + 1/2 t) = (1/2 T + 1/2 t)² = 1/4 TT + 1/2 Tt + 1/4 tt, the same 1 : 2 : 1 genotypic ratio obtained from the Punnett square.
solution.why_others_wrong: 1/2 TT + 1/2 tt and 3/4 TT + 1/4 tt drop the 2ab (Tt) term; 1/4 TT + 1/4 Tt + 1/2 tt misplaces the coefficients of the expansion.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Principles of Inheritance and Variation', inheritance of one gene: law of segregation
solution.final_answer: Option A: (1/2 T + 1/2 t)² = 1/4 TT + 1/2 Tt + 1/4 tt

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: NCERT's example of incomplete dominance is the inheritance of flower colour in the dog flower (snapdragon). The dog flower belongs to the genus:

solution.explanation: NCERT: the inheritance of flower colour in the dog flower (snapdragon or Antirrhinum sp.) is a good example to understand incomplete dominance: RR (red) × rr (white) gives pink (Rr) F1 plants.
solution.why_others_wrong: Pisum is the garden pea used by Mendel; Rauwolfia is NCERT's example of genetic diversity (reserpine); Mirabilis is not the snapdragon.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Principles of Inheritance and Variation', inheritance of one gene: incomplete dominance
solution.final_answer: Option C: Antirrhinum

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: NCERT describes phenylketonuria, in which the affected individual lacks an enzyme that converts phenylalanine into tyrosine, as:

options.text: A chromosomal disorder caused by trisomy of chromosome 21
A sex-linked dominant disorder carried on the Y chromosome
A disorder caused by an increase in a whole set of chromosomes
An inborn error of metabolism, inherited as an autosomal recessive trait

solution.explanation: NCERT: phenylketonuria is an inborn error of metabolism that is also inherited as an autosomal recessive trait. The affected individual lacks an enzyme that converts the amino acid phenylalanine into tyrosine; phenylalanine accumulates and is converted into phenylpyruvic acid and other derivatives.
steps: Inborn error of metabolism, autosomal recessive
solution.why_others_wrong: Trisomy of chromosome 21 is Down's syndrome; PKU is not sex-linked; an increase in a whole set of chromosomes is polyploidy.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Principles of Inheritance and Variation', genetic disorders: Mendelian disorders
solution.final_answer: Option D: An inborn error of metabolism, inherited as an autosomal recessive trait

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Mendel published his work in 1865, but it remained unrecognised till 1900. Which of the following does NCERT give as one of the reasons?

options.text: His experiments were based on too small a sample of plants
Communication was not easy in those days, and his work could not be widely publicised
His results were contradicted by Morgan's experiments on Drosophila
He studied characters that did not show contrasting traits

solution.explanation: NCERT gives several reasons: communication was not easy (as it is now) in those days and his work could not be widely publicised; his concept of factors as stable and discrete units was not accepted as an explanation for the apparently continuous variation seen in nature; the use of mathematics to explain biological phenomena was new and unacceptable to many biologists; and he could not provide any physical proof for the existence of factors.
solution.why_others_wrong: NCERT credits Mendel with a large sampling size and with characters showing contrasting traits; Morgan's work came decades later and supported, not contradicted, Mendelian inheritance.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Principles of Inheritance and Variation', inheritance of two genes: chromosomal theory of inheritance
solution.final_answer: Option B: Communication was not easy in those days, and his work could not be widely publicised

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: In snapdragon, red-flowered (RR) and white-flowered (rr) plants give pink-flowered F1 plants. The F1 plants are self-pollinated and 400 F2 plants are raised. How many of these are expected to have pink flowers?

solution.explanation: Rr × Rr gives 1/4 RR (red) : 1/2 Rr (pink) : 1/4 rr (white). Pink = 1/2 × 400 = 200.
solution.why_others_wrong: 100 is the number of red (or white) plants; 300 treats pink as a dominant phenotype (3/4); 400 assumes the F2 stays uniform like the F1.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Principles of Inheritance and Variation', inheritance of one gene: incomplete dominance
solution.final_answer: Option C: 200

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Haemophilia is transmitted from an unaffected carrier female to some of the male progeny.
Reason (R): In haemophilia, a single protein that is a part of the cascade of proteins involved in the clotting of blood is affected.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.concept: Haemophilia: pattern of transmission versus molecular defect
solution.explanation: NCERT: haemophilia is a sex-linked recessive disease that shows its transmission from an unaffected carrier female to some of the male progeny (A true). In this disease a single protein of the clotting cascade is affected, so a simple cut results in non-stop bleeding (R true). R explains the symptom, not the pattern of transmission, which follows from the gene being on the X chromosome.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Principles of Inheritance and Variation', genetic disorders: Mendelian disorders — haemophilia
solution.final_answer: Option B: Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Match List-I (genotype) with List-II (phenotype).

List-I:
A. Rr in snapdragon
B. IᴬIᴮ
C. Iᴬi
D. ii

List-II:
I. Blood group O
II. Pink flowers
III. Blood group A
IV. Blood group AB

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.concept: Genotype to phenotype under different dominance relations
solution.explanation: Snapdragon Rr is pink (incomplete dominance) (A-II). Iᴬ and Iᴮ are co-dominant, so IᴬIᴮ is blood group AB (B-IV). Iᴬ is dominant over i, so Iᴬi is blood group A (C-III). i produces no sugar, so ii is blood group O (D-I).
solution.why_others_wrong: The wrong codes give IᴬIᴮ blood group A and Iᴬi blood group AB, make Rr blood group AB, or interchange the A and O groups.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Principles of Inheritance and Variation', inheritance of one gene: incomplete dominance; co-dominance
solution.final_answer: Option D: A-II, B-IV, C-III, D-I

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: In sickle-cell anaemia, the mutant haemoglobin molecule undergoes polymerisation, which changes the shape of the RBC from a biconcave disc to an elongated sickle-like structure. According to NCERT, this happens under:

solution.explanation: NCERT: the mutant haemoglobin molecule undergoes polymerisation under low oxygen tension, causing the change in the shape of the RBC from biconcave disc to elongated sickle-like structure.
steps: Hbˢ polymerises at low O₂ tension
solution.why_others_wrong: NCERT links sickling to low, not high, oxygen tension; it does not attribute sickling to body temperature or to UV light.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Principles of Inheritance and Variation', genetic disorders: Mendelian disorders — sickle-cell anaemia
solution.final_answer: Option A: Low oxygen tension

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Loss (deletion) or gain (insertion or duplication) of a segment of DNA results in alteration in chromosomes.
Reason (R): The DNA helix runs continuously from one end to the other in each chromatid, in a highly supercoiled form.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: NCERT (mutation): since the DNA helix runs continuously from one end to the other in each chromatid, in a highly supercoiled form, loss (deletion) or gain (insertion/duplication) of a segment of DNA results in alteration in chromosomes. R is the reason NCERT gives for A.
steps: A chromatid = one continuous supercoiled DNA helix
So changing a DNA segment changes the chromosome
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Principles of Inheritance and Variation', mutation
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: A pea plant heterozygous for seed shape and seed colour (RrYy; the two genes assort independently) is self-pollinated, and 1600 seeds are obtained. How many seeds are expected to be heterozygous for exactly one of the two genes?

solution.concept: Genotype classes in a dihybrid F2
solution.explanation: For each gene, Rr × Rr gives 1/2 heterozygous and 1/2 homozygous (likewise for Y). Exactly one heterozygous = P(Rr)·P(YY or yy) + P(RR or rr)·P(Yy) = 1/2·1/2 + 1/2·1/2 = 1/2. Expected = 1/2 × 1600 = 800.
solution.shortcut: Exactly one of two independent 1/2 events: 2 × 1/4 = 1/2.
solution.why_others_wrong: 400 counts seeds heterozygous for both genes (1/4); 1200 counts seeds heterozygous for at least one gene (3/4); 200 counts only one of the two ways (e.g. Rr with homozygous Y) and halves it again.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Principles of Inheritance and Variation', inheritance of two genes: law of independent assortment
solution.final_answer: Option D: 800

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Match List-I (cross) with List-II (ratio expected among the progeny).

List-I:
A. Rr × Rr in snapdragon (flower colours)
B. Iᴬi × Iᴮi (blood groups)
C. Tt × Tt in pea (phenotypes)
D. Tt × tt in pea (phenotypes)

List-II:
I. 3 : 1
II. 1 : 1 : 1 : 1
III. 1 : 1
IV. 1 : 2 : 1

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: Snapdragon Rr × Rr: red : pink : white = 1 : 2 : 1 (A-IV). Iᴬi × Iᴮi: IᴬIᴮ (AB), Iᴬi (A), Iᴮi (B) and ii (O) each 1/4, i.e. 1 : 1 : 1 : 1 (B-II). Pea Tt × Tt with complete dominance: tall : dwarf = 3 : 1 (C-I). Tt × tt (test cross): tall : dwarf = 1 : 1 (D-III).
solution.why_others_wrong: The wrong codes give the snapdragon F2 the 3 : 1 ratio of complete dominance, give the blood-group cross 3 : 1, or interchange the monohybrid F2 and the test cross.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Principles of Inheritance and Variation', inheritance of one gene
solution.final_answer: Option B: A-IV, B-II, C-I, D-III

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Individuals with Down's syndrome have 47 chromosomes in their somatic cells.
Reason (R): Down's syndrome results from polyploidy, an increase in a whole set of chromosomes.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: NCERT: Down's syndrome is caused by the presence of an additional copy of chromosome 21 (trisomy of 21), so the cells have 46 + 1 = 47 chromosomes (A true). This gain of a single chromosome is aneuploidy, which results from failure of segregation of chromatids; polyploidy (an increase in a whole set of chromosomes, from failure of cytokinesis) is often seen in plants. R is false.
steps: One extra chromosome = aneuploidy, not polyploidy
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Principles of Inheritance and Variation', genetic disorders: chromosomal disorders
solution.final_answer: Option C: A is true but R is false.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): A cross between a pink-flowered and a red-flowered snapdragon gives no white-flowered offspring.
Reason (R): Every offspring of this cross receives an R allele from the red-flowered (RR) parent.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.concept: Predicting a cross under incomplete dominance
solution.explanation: Red is RR and pink is Rr. Every gamete of the red parent carries R, so every offspring is RR (red) or Rr (pink), in a 1 : 1 ratio. A white flower needs rr, which requires r from both parents; because each offspring gets R from the red parent, rr cannot arise. R therefore explains A.
steps: Offspring RR or Rr → red or pink
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Principles of Inheritance and Variation', inheritance of one gene: incomplete dominance
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
For which of the following can the genotype be stated with certainty from the phenotype alone?

(a) A person with blood group AB
(b) A person with blood group O
(c) A person with blood group A
(d) A pink-flowered snapdragon
(e) A tall pea plant

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: Blood group AB arises only from IᴬIᴮ (co-dominance) (a), and blood group O only from ii (b). A pink snapdragon must be Rr, since under incomplete dominance the heterozygote has its own phenotype (d). Blood group A may be IᴬIᴬ or Iᴬi (c), and a tall pea plant may be TT or Tt (e) — which is why a test cross is needed to find the genotype of a plant with the dominant phenotype.
steps: A → IᴬIᴬ or Iᴬi; tall → TT or Tt
solution.why_others_wrong: Blood group A (c) and tall (e) each correspond to two genotypes, so options containing them are wrong; '(a), (d) and (e)' also omits blood group O.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Principles of Inheritance and Variation', inheritance of one gene: co-dominance; incomplete dominance; test cross
solution.final_answer: Option B: (a), (b) and (d) only

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: In humans, each pregnancy has an equal (50 per cent) chance of producing a male or a female child. A couple has four children. What is the probability that exactly two of them are sons and two are daughters, in any order of birth?

solution.concept: Probability of a mix of sons and daughters
solution.explanation: NCERT: in each pregnancy there is always a 50 per cent probability of a male or a female child. For four children there are 2⁴ = 16 equally likely birth orders. The number of orders with exactly two sons is 4C2 = 6, so the probability is 6/16 = 3/8.
solution.why_others_wrong: 1/2 assumes 'half sons' is the most likely outcome with probability 1/2; 1/16 counts only one particular order; 1/4 has no basis in the count of orders.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Principles of Inheritance and Variation', sex determination: sex determination in humans
solution.final_answer: Option C: 3/8

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Among the seven pairs of contrasting traits of garden pea studied by Mendel, in how many characters is the DOMINANT trait a colour?

solution.explanation: NCERT's table: stem height (tall/dwarf), flower colour (violet/white), flower position (axial/terminal), pod shape (inflated/constricted), pod colour (green/yellow), seed shape (round/wrinkled) and seed colour (yellow/green). The dominant trait is a colour for flower colour (violet), pod colour (green) and seed colour (yellow): three characters.
solution.why_others_wrong: Height, flower position, pod shape and seed shape have non-colour dominant traits (tall, axial, inflated, round), so the count is neither one, two nor four.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Principles of Inheritance and Variation', Mendel's laws of inheritance (contrasting traits studied by Mendel in pea)
solution.final_answer: Option D: Three

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Klinefelter's syndrome is caused by the absence of one of the X chromosomes.
Statement II: Turner's syndrome is caused by the absence of one of the X chromosomes, i.e. 45 with X0.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: NCERT: Klinefelter's syndrome is caused by the presence of an additional copy of the X chromosome, resulting in the karyotype 47, XXY (Statement I false). Turner's syndrome is caused by the absence of one of the X chromosomes, i.e. 45 with X0; such females are sterile (Statement II true).
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Principles of Inheritance and Variation', genetic disorders: chromosomal disorders
solution.final_answer: Option D: Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Take NCERT's model of human skin colour controlled by three genes A, B and C, in which every dominant allele adds equally to the colour. A person of genotype AaBbCc marries a person of genotype AABBcc. What fraction of their children are expected to carry exactly four dominant alleles?

solution.concept: Additive alleles with one parent of fixed contribution
solution.explanation: Every gamete of the AABBcc parent is ABc, carrying two dominant alleles. The AaBbCc parent passes 0–3 dominant alleles, each gene independently with probability 1/2, giving 1/8, 3/8, 3/8, 1/8 for 0, 1, 2, 3. A child with four dominant alleles needs exactly two from the AaBbCc parent: probability 3C2/8 = 3/8.
solution.why_others_wrong: 15/64 is the answer for AaBbCc × AaBbCc; 1/8 is the chance of three dominant alleles from the heterozygous parent (five in all); 1/4 does not follow from the binomial distribution.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Principles of Inheritance and Variation', polygenic inheritance
solution.final_answer: Option A: 3/8

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: A woman with normal vision who is a carrier of red-green colour blindness marries a man with normal colour vision. They have two children. What is the probability that one of them is a colour-blind son and the other is a carrier daughter, in either order of birth?

solution.explanation: For each child: P(son) = 1/2 and a son is colour blind if he gets the mother's affected X (1/2), so P(colour-blind son) = 1/4. P(daughter) = 1/2, and every daughter gets the father's normal X; she is a carrier if she gets the mother's affected X (1/2), so P(carrier daughter) = 1/4. Two orders are possible: 2 × (1/4 × 1/4) = 1/8.
solution.why_others_wrong: 1/16 takes only one birth order; 1/4 is the probability for a single child of one type; 1/2 is the chance that a son is colour blind, not the combined probability.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Principles of Inheritance and Variation', genetic disorders: Mendelian disorders — colour blindness
solution.final_answer: Option B: 1/8

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Match List-I (change in a plant whose normal somatic cells have 2n = 14) with List-II (chromosome number of the resulting somatic cells).

List-I:
A. Gain of one chromosome (aneuploidy)
B. Loss of one chromosome (aneuploidy)
C. Increase by one whole set, to three sets (polyploidy)
D. Increase by two whole sets, to four sets (polyploidy)

List-II:
I. 28
II. 13
III. 21
IV. 15

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.concept: Counting chromosomes in aneuploids and polyploids
solution.explanation: NCERT: failure of segregation of chromatids gives the gain or loss of a chromosome(s) (aneuploidy); failure of cytokinesis after telophase gives an increase in a whole set of chromosomes (polyploidy), often seen in plants. With 2n = 14, one set (n) = 7: 14 + 1 = 15 (A-IV), 14 − 1 = 13 (B-II), three sets = 21 (C-III) and four sets = 28 (D-I).
solution.why_others_wrong: The wrong codes swap gain with loss of a chromosome, three sets with four sets, or confuse 13 with 21.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Principles of Inheritance and Variation', mutation; genetic disorders: chromosomal disorders
solution.final_answer: Option C: A-IV, B-II, C-III, D-I

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): A man with blood group AB and a woman with blood group O can have children with blood group A or B only.
Reason (R): The allele Iᴬ is completely dominant over the allele Iᴮ.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: The man (IᴬIᴮ) gives Iᴬ or Iᴮ and the woman (ii) gives i, so the children are Iᴬi (A) or Iᴮi (B) in equal numbers; groups AB and O cannot occur (A true). NCERT: Iᴬ and Iᴮ are co-dominant — when present together, both express their own type of sugar, giving AB. Neither is dominant over the other, so R is false.
steps: Iᴬ and Iᴮ: co-dominant, both dominant over i
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Principles of Inheritance and Variation', inheritance of one gene: co-dominance
solution.final_answer: Option C: A is true but R is false.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: In the F2 of Mendel's dihybrid cross (RRYY × rryy, F1 self-pollinated), round and wrinkled seeds occur in the ratio 3 : 1, just as in a monohybrid cross.
Statement II: Among the wrinkled seeds of this F2, yellow and green seeds occur in equal numbers.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: The F2 is 9 round yellow : 3 round green : 3 wrinkled yellow : 1 wrinkled green. Round : wrinkled = (9 + 3) : (3 + 1) = 12 : 4 = 3 : 1, the monohybrid ratio, because the two genes assort independently (Statement I true). Among the wrinkled seeds, yellow : green = 3 : 1, not 1 : 1 (Statement II false).
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Principles of Inheritance and Variation', inheritance of two genes: law of independent assortment
solution.final_answer: Option C: Statement I is true but Statement II is false.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Consider four species in each of which the diploid female has 20 chromosomes in her somatic cells. Sex is determined in them by the XO, XY, ZW and haplodiploid mechanisms described in NCERT, respectively. Which of the following statements are correct?

(a) In the XO species, a somatic cell of the male has 19 chromosomes.
(b) In the XY species, a somatic cell of the male has 20 chromosomes.
(c) In the haplodiploid species, the male has 10 chromosomes.
(d) In the ZW species, a somatic cell of the female has 19 chromosomes.
(e) In the XO species, every sperm carries 10 chromosomes.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: XO type (grasshopper): females have a pair of X chromosomes, males only one X, so the male has 20 − 1 = 19 (a), and half the sperms carry the X (10 chromosomes) while half lack it (9), so (e) is false. XY type: males have X and Y, so both sexes have 20 (b). ZW type (birds): the female has one Z and one W, so she still has 20 (d false). Haplodiploidy (honey bee): males develop from unfertilised eggs and are haploid, with 10 (c).
steps: ZW female: Z + W, equal numbers
solution.why_others_wrong: (d) forgets that the ZW female has a W chromosome, and (e) ignores the sperms that lack the X, so every option containing them is wrong.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Principles of Inheritance and Variation', sex determination
solution.final_answer: Option A: (a), (b) and (c) only

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Two parents who both have blood group O can have a child with blood group A.
Reason (R): The allele i does not produce any sugar.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: Blood group O is ii, so both parents can pass only i, and every child is ii (blood group O); A is false. NCERT: the allele i does not produce any sugar, whereas Iᴬ and Iᴮ produce slightly different forms of the sugar (R true).
steps: O × O = ii × ii → all ii
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Principles of Inheritance and Variation', inheritance of one gene: co-dominance
solution.final_answer: Option D: A is false but R is true.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Two parents with normal phenotype are both heterozygous carriers of phenylketonuria. Which of the following statements are correct?

(a) Each of their children has a 1/4 chance of being affected.
(b) An affected child lacks the enzyme that converts the amino acid phenylalanine into tyrosine.
(c) In an affected child, phenylalanine is converted into phenylpyruvic acid and other derivatives, whose accumulation in the brain results in mental retardation.
(d) Only their sons can be affected, because the trait is sex-linked.
(e) All their children with normal phenotype will be carriers.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: PKU is an autosomal recessive trait, so Pp × Pp gives 1/4 PP, 1/2 Pp and 1/4 pp; each child has a 1/4 chance of being affected (a), sons and daughters alike (d false). Children with normal phenotype are PP or Pp, so not all are carriers (e false). NCERT: the affected individual lacks an enzyme that converts phenylalanine into tyrosine (b); phenylalanine accumulates and is converted into phenylpyruvic acid and other derivatives, whose accumulation in the brain results in mental retardation (c).
solution.why_others_wrong: (d) makes an autosomal trait sex-linked and (e) ignores the normal homozygous (PP) children, so every option containing either is wrong.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Principles of Inheritance and Variation', genetic disorders: Mendelian disorders — phenylketonuria
solution.final_answer: Option B: (a), (b) and (c) only

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: During transcription, the DNA strand with 5'→3' polarity, whose sequence is the same as that of the RNA (except for thymine in place of uracil), is displaced. NCERT notes that this strand, strangely, does not code for anything, yet it is called the:

solution.explanation: NCERT: in a transcription unit, the strand with 3'→5' polarity acts as the template. The other strand, which has 5'→3' polarity and the same sequence as the RNA (except thymine at the place of uracil), is displaced during transcription. Strangely, this strand (which does not code for anything) is referred to as the coding strand.
steps: Coding strand: 5'→3', same sequence as RNA, displaced
solution.why_others_wrong: The template strand is the one copied into RNA; leading and lagging strands are terms for the new strands made during DNA replication.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Molecular Basis of Inheritance', transcription: transcription unit
solution.final_answer: Option D: Coding strand

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: According to NCERT, the cellular factory responsible for synthesising proteins, which consists of structural RNAs and about 80 different proteins, is the:

solution.explanation: NCERT: the cellular factory responsible for synthesising proteins is the ribosome. The ribosome consists of structural RNAs and about 80 different proteins. In its inactive state it exists as two subunits, a large and a small one.
solution.why_others_wrong: A nucleosome is DNA wrapped round a histone octamer; the Golgi apparatus packages materials; the nucleolus is a site of rRNA synthesis, not the factory that synthesises proteins.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Molecular Basis of Inheritance', translation
solution.final_answer: Option A: Ribosome

questions.subject: Botany
questions.subtopic: Human genome project and DNA fingerprinting
questions.question_text: In the Human Genome Project, the random DNA fragments were cloned using specialised vectors called BAC and YAC. According to NCERT, the commonly used hosts for this cloning were:

solution.explanation: NCERT: the random fragments were cloned in suitable hosts using specialised vectors; cloning amplified each piece so that it could be sequenced with ease. The commonly used hosts were bacteria and yeast, and the vectors were called BAC (bacterial artificial chromosomes) and YAC (yeast artificial chromosomes).
solution.why_others_wrong: The vector names themselves (bacterial and yeast artificial chromosomes) point to the hosts; NCERT does not name mammalian cells, plants, fungi other than yeast, phages or protozoans as hosts.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Molecular Basis of Inheritance', human genome project: methodologies
solution.final_answer: Option C: Bacteria and yeast

questions.subject: Botany
questions.subtopic: Human genome project and DNA fingerprinting
questions.question_text: According to NCERT, polymorphism in DNA sequence is the basis of:

options.text: The universality of the genetic code
Genetic mapping of the human genome as well as DNA fingerprinting

solution.explanation: NCERT: polymorphism (variation at the genetic level) arises due to mutations; an inheritable mutation observed in a population at high frequency is DNA polymorphism. Polymorphism in DNA sequence is the basis of genetic mapping of the human genome as well as of DNA fingerprinting.
solution.why_others_wrong: The universality of the code, semiconservative replication and nucleosome formation are shared by all individuals; they do not depend on variation between them.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Molecular Basis of Inheritance', DNA fingerprinting
solution.final_answer: Option B: Genetic mapping of the human genome as well as DNA fingerprinting

questions.subject: Botany
questions.subtopic: Human genome project and DNA fingerprinting
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: In a VNTR, a small DNA sequence is arranged tandemly in many copy numbers, and the copy number varies from chromosome to chromosome in an individual.
Statement II: The numbers of repeats in VNTRs show a very high degree of polymorphism.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: NCERT: the VNTR belongs to a class of satellite DNA referred to as mini-satellite. A small DNA sequence is arranged tandemly in many copy numbers. The copy number varies from chromosome to chromosome in an individual (Statement I true). The numbers of repeat show a very high degree of polymorphism, and as a result the size of VNTR varies from 0.1 to 20 kb (Statement II true).
steps: VNTR = tandem repeats, copy number varies
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Molecular Basis of Inheritance', DNA fingerprinting
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Match List-I (gene of the lac operon) with List-II (its product).

List-I:
A. i gene
B. z gene
C. y gene
D. a gene

List-II:
I. Transacetylase
II. Repressor
III. Permease
IV. β-galactosidase

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: NCERT: the lac operon consists of one regulatory gene (the i gene, coding for the repressor) and three structural genes: z codes for β-galactosidase, which hydrolyses lactose into galactose and glucose; y codes for permease, which increases the permeability of the cell to β-galactosides; and a codes for transacetylase.
solution.why_others_wrong: The wrong codes swap the repressor with β-galactosidase, β-galactosidase with permease, or permease with transacetylase.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Molecular Basis of Inheritance', regulation of gene expression: the lac operon
solution.final_answer: Option D: A-II, B-IV, C-III, D-I

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): In eukaryotes, DNA replication takes place in the S-phase of the cell cycle.
Reason (R): The 2'-OH group present at every nucleotide in RNA makes RNA labile and easily degradable.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: NCERT: in eukaryotes, the replication of DNA takes place at the S-phase of the cell cycle (A true). The 2'-OH group present at every nucleotide in RNA is a reactive group that makes RNA labile and easily degradable (R true). R is about the chemistry of RNA and has nothing to do with the timing of DNA replication.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Molecular Basis of Inheritance', replication; the search for genetic material: properties of genetic material
solution.final_answer: Option B: Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: RNA acts as the genetic material in some viruses and mostly functions as a messenger. According to NCERT, RNA has additional roles as well. It also functions as:

options.text: The main store of genetic information in most organisms
A positively charged packaging protein around which DNA is wrapped
An adapter, a structural and in some cases a catalytic molecule
The template for DNA replication in all cells

solution.explanation: NCERT: DNA acts as the genetic material in most organisms. RNA, though it also acts as the genetic material in some viruses, mostly functions as a messenger. RNA has additional roles as well: it functions as adapter, structural, and in some cases as a catalytic molecule.
solution.why_others_wrong: DNA, not RNA, is the main genetic material and the template for DNA replication; DNA is wrapped round positively charged histone proteins, not round RNA.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Molecular Basis of Inheritance', introduction; the RNA world
solution.final_answer: Option C: An adapter, a structural and in some cases a catalytic molecule

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): In the Meselson and Stahl experiment, DNA containing ¹⁵N was distinguished from DNA containing ¹⁴N by density, not by detecting radioactivity.
Reason (R): ¹⁵N is not a radioactive isotope; it can be separated from ¹⁴N only on the basis of densities.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.concept: ¹⁵N is a heavy, non-radioactive isotope
solution.explanation: NCERT: Meselson and Stahl grew E. coli in a medium containing ¹⁵NH₄Cl as the only nitrogen source, so that ¹⁵N was incorporated into newly synthesised DNA. Heavy DNA was distinguished from normal DNA by centrifugation in a caesium chloride density gradient. NCERT notes that ¹⁵N is not a radioactive isotope and can be separated from ¹⁴N only based on densities — which is exactly why density, not radioactivity, was used.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Molecular Basis of Inheritance', replication: the experimental proof
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): In long DNA molecules, replication occurs within a small opening of the DNA helix, the replication fork.
Reason (R): The two strands of a long DNA molecule cannot be separated in their entire length because of the very high energy requirement.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: NCERT: for long DNA molecules, since the two strands of DNA cannot be separated in their entire length (due to very high energy requirement), replication occurs within a small opening of the DNA helix, referred to as the replication fork. R is the reason given for A.
steps: Separating the whole length: too much energy
So replication proceeds at a small opening — the fork
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Molecular Basis of Inheritance', replication: the machinery and the enzymes
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Avery, MacLeod and McCarty purified biochemicals such as proteins, DNA and RNA from heat-killed S cells to see which of them could transform live R cells into S cells.
Statement II: Avery, MacLeod and McCarty concluded that DNA is the hereditary material, but not all biologists were convinced.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.concept: The work of Avery, MacLeod and McCarty
solution.explanation: NCERT: Oswald Avery, Colin MacLeod and Maclyn McCarty (1933–44) worked to determine the biochemical nature of the 'transforming principle'. They purified biochemicals (proteins, DNA, RNA, etc.) from the heat-killed S cells to see which ones could transform live R cells into S cells (Statement I true). They discovered that DNA alone from S bacteria caused R bacteria to become transformed and concluded that DNA is the hereditary material, but not all biologists were convinced (Statement II true). The unequivocal proof came later from Hershey and Chase.
steps: Purified S-cell biochemicals tested on live R cells
Concluded DNA; not all were convinced
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Molecular Basis of Inheritance', the search for genetic material: biochemical characterisation of transforming principle
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Each operon has its specific operator and specific repressor.
Statement II: The lac repressor can also bind to the operators of other operons, such as the trp operon, and switch them off.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: NCERT: each operon has its specific operator and specific repressor. For example, the lac operator is present only in the lac operon and it interacts specifically with the lac repressor only (Statement I true). So the lac repressor does not act on the operators of other operons such as trp, ara, his or val (Statement II false).
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Molecular Basis of Inheritance', regulation of gene expression: the lac operon
solution.final_answer: Option C: Statement I is true but Statement II is false.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Which of the following arranges these investigations in the chronological order in which NCERT dates them?

options.text: Avery, MacLeod and McCarty → Griffith → Hershey and Chase → Meselson and Stahl
Griffith's transformation experiments → work of Avery, MacLeod and McCarty → Hershey and Chase's bacteriophage experiments → Meselson and Stahl's proof of semiconservative replication
Griffith → Hershey and Chase → Avery, MacLeod and McCarty → Meselson and Stahl
Griffith → Avery, MacLeod and McCarty → Meselson and Stahl → Hershey and Chase

solution.concept: History of the search for the genetic material
solution.explanation: NCERT dates Griffith's experiments to 1928, the work of Avery, MacLeod and McCarty to 1933–44, Hershey and Chase's experiments to 1952 and Meselson and Stahl's experiment to 1958. Avery and colleagues worked on the 'transforming principle' that Griffith had described, and Hershey and Chase then gave the unequivocal proof that DNA is the genetic material.
solution.why_others_wrong: Avery's group studied Griffith's transforming principle, so it could not come first; Hershey and Chase (1952) came after Avery's work and before Meselson and Stahl (1958).
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Molecular Basis of Inheritance', the search for genetic material; replication
solution.final_answer: Option B: Griffith's transformation experiments → work of Avery, MacLeod and McCarty → Hershey and Chase's bacteriophage experiments → Meselson and Stahl's proof of semiconservative replication

questions.subject: Botany
questions.subtopic: Human genome project and DNA fingerprinting
questions.question_text: Which of the following gives the correct order of the steps in DNA fingerprinting as listed in NCERT?

options.text: Isolation of DNA → electrophoresis → digestion by restriction endonucleases → hybridisation with a labelled VNTR probe → blotting → autoradiography
Isolation of DNA → digestion by restriction endonucleases → blotting → electrophoresis → autoradiography → hybridisation with a labelled VNTR probe
Digestion by restriction endonucleases → isolation of DNA → electrophoresis → blotting → hybridisation with a labelled VNTR probe → autoradiography

Isolation of DNA → digestion by restriction endonucleases → separation of fragments by electrophoresis → blotting onto nitrocellulose or nylon membranes → hybridisation with a labelled VNTR probe → detection by autoradiography

solution.explanation: NCERT lists the steps as (i) isolation of DNA, (ii) digestion of DNA by restriction endonucleases, (iii) separation of DNA fragments by electrophoresis, (iv) transferring (blotting) of the separated fragments to synthetic membranes such as nitrocellulose or nylon, (v) hybridisation using a labelled VNTR probe, and (vi) detection of hybridised DNA fragments by autoradiography.
solution.why_others_wrong: DNA must be isolated before it can be cut, and cut before the fragments can be separated; blotting follows electrophoresis, and autoradiography detects the fragments only after hybridisation with the probe.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Molecular Basis of Inheritance', DNA fingerprinting
solution.final_answer: Option D: Isolation of DNA → digestion by restriction endonucleases → separation of fragments by electrophoresis → blotting onto nitrocellulose or nylon membranes → hybridisation with a labelled VNTR probe → detection by autoradiography

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
NCERT names the nucleosides adenosine or deoxyadenosine, guanosine or deoxyguanosine, cytidine or deoxycytidine, and uridine or deoxythymidine. Which of the following nucleosides contain a pyrimidine base?

(a) Cytidine
(b) Uridine
(c) Deoxythymidine
(d) Adenosine
(e) Deoxyguanosine

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: A nucleoside is a nitrogenous base linked to a pentose sugar by an N-glycosidic linkage. NCERT: the purines are adenine and guanine; the pyrimidines are cytosine, uracil and thymine. Cytidine (cytosine), uridine (uracil) and deoxythymidine (thymine) therefore contain pyrimidines, whereas adenosine (adenine) and deoxyguanosine (guanine) contain purines.
steps: Pyrimidines: C, U, T → cytidine, uridine, deoxythymidine
solution.why_others_wrong: Adenosine and deoxyguanosine contain the purines adenine and guanine, so every option containing (d) or (e) is wrong.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Molecular Basis of Inheritance', the DNA: structure of polynucleotide chain
solution.final_answer: Option B: (a), (b) and (c) only

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Match List-I (factor or enzyme) with List-II (its role).

List-I:
A. DNA ligase
B. Initiation factor (σ)
C. Termination factor (ρ)
D. Release factor

List-II:
I. Terminates translation at a stop codon
II. Joins the discontinuously synthesised DNA fragments
III. Helps RNA polymerase to terminate transcription
IV. Helps RNA polymerase to initiate transcription

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: NCERT: the discontinuously synthesised fragments of DNA are later joined by DNA ligase (A-II). In bacteria, RNA polymerase associates transiently with the initiation factor σ to initiate transcription (B-IV) and with the termination factor ρ to terminate it (C-III). At the end of translation, a release factor binds to the stop codon, terminating translation and releasing the polypeptide from the ribosome (D-I).
solution.why_others_wrong: The wrong codes interchange σ and ρ, ρ and the release factor (one ends transcription, the other translation), or ligase and σ.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Molecular Basis of Inheritance', replication; transcription; translation
solution.final_answer: Option B: A-II, B-IV, C-III, D-I

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Heterochromatin is the loosely packed region of chromatin that stains light.
Reason (R): Euchromatin is said to be transcriptionally active chromatin.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: NCERT: in some regions chromatin is loosely packed and stains light; this is euchromatin, which is transcriptionally active (R true). In other regions chromatin is densely packed and stains dark; this is heterochromatin, which is inactive. A attributes the features of euchromatin to heterochromatin, so A is false.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Molecular Basis of Inheritance', packaging of DNA helix
solution.final_answer: Option D: A is false but R is true.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: In E. coli, if the bacteria do not have lactose around them to be utilised as an energy source, they no longer require the synthesis of the enzyme β-galactosidase.
Statement II: In eukaryotes, the expression of genes is regulated only at the transcriptional level.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: NCERT: in E. coli, β-galactosidase catalyses the hydrolysis of lactose into galactose and glucose; if the bacteria do not have lactose around them to be utilised for energy, they no longer require the synthesis of this enzyme (Statement I true). In eukaryotes, regulation can be exerted at the transcriptional level (formation of the primary transcript), the processing level (regulation of splicing), the transport of mRNA from nucleus to cytoplasm, and the translational level (Statement II false).
steps: Enzyme made only when its substrate is available
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Molecular Basis of Inheritance', regulation of gene expression
solution.final_answer: Option C: Statement I is true but Statement II is false.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): In eukaryotes, RNA polymerase I transcribes the rRNAs 28S, 18S and 5.8S.
Reason (R): RNA polymerase I also transcribes the 5S rRNA.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.concept: Division of labour among eukaryotic RNA polymerases
solution.explanation: NCERT: in the nucleus there are at least three RNA polymerases. RNA polymerase I transcribes rRNAs (28S, 18S and 5.8S) (A true); RNA polymerase III is responsible for transcription of tRNA, 5S rRNA and snRNAs; RNA polymerase II transcribes the precursor of mRNA, the hnRNA. Since the 5S rRNA is made by RNA polymerase III, R is false.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Molecular Basis of Inheritance', transcription: transcription in eukaryotes
solution.final_answer: Option C: A is true but R is false.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): A typical nucleosome contains about 2000 bp of DNA helix.
Reason (R): Under the electron microscope, nucleosomes in chromatin are seen as 'beads-on-string'.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: NCERT: the positively charged histone octamer has the negatively charged DNA wrapped around it to form the nucleosome; a typical nucleosome contains 200 bp of DNA helix, not 2000 bp (A false). Nucleosomes constitute the repeating unit of a structure in the nucleus called chromatin, which is seen as 'beads-on-string' under the electron microscope (R true).
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Molecular Basis of Inheritance', packaging of DNA helix
solution.final_answer: Option D: A is false but R is true.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: NCERT lists nucleosides in pairs: adenosine or deoxyadenosine, guanosine or deoxyguanosine, cytidine or deoxycytidine, and uridine or deoxythymidine. Which of the following pairs contain the SAME nitrogenous base and differ only in their sugar?

solution.explanation: Adenosine (adenine + ribose) and deoxyadenosine (adenine + deoxyribose) share the base and differ only in the sugar. Uridine and deoxythymidine, although paired in NCERT's list, contain different bases — uracil in RNA and thymine (5-methyl uracil) in DNA — as well as different sugars. Cytidine and guanosine, and deoxyguanosine and deoxyadenosine, contain different bases.
steps: Same base, different sugar: adenosine / deoxyadenosine
solution.why_others_wrong: Uridine and deoxythymidine differ in base (uracil versus thymine); cytidine/guanosine and deoxyguanosine/deoxyadenosine pair a pyrimidine with a purine or two different purines.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Molecular Basis of Inheritance', the DNA: structure of polynucleotide chain
solution.final_answer: Option A: Adenosine and deoxyadenosine

questions.subject: Botany
questions.subtopic: Human genome project and DNA fingerprinting
questions.question_text: Which of the following gives the correct order of the steps in the methodology of sequencing the human genome, as described in NCERT?

options.text: Whole chromosome sequenced intact → cut into random fragments → fragments cloned in BAC or YAC vectors → overlapping regions aligned by computer programs
Total DNA isolated → fragments arranged on the basis of overlapping regions → fragments cloned in bacteria or yeast → fragments sequenced by automated DNA sequencers
Total DNA isolated and broken into random fragments → fragments sequenced by automated DNA sequencers → fragments cloned in bacteria or yeast to amplify them → sequences annotated

Total DNA isolated and broken into random fragments → fragments cloned in bacteria or yeast using BAC or YAC vectors → fragments sequenced by automated DNA sequencers → sequences arranged on the basis of overlapping regions using computer programs → sequences annotated and assigned to chromosomes

solution.explanation: NCERT: the total DNA from a cell was isolated and converted into random fragments of relatively smaller sizes (very long pieces cannot be sequenced). These were cloned in suitable hosts (bacteria and yeast) using BAC and YAC vectors, which amplified each piece so that it could be sequenced with ease. The fragments were sequenced using automated DNA sequencers working on Sanger's method. The sequences were then arranged on the basis of overlapping regions, using specialised computer-based programs, and were subsequently annotated and assigned to each chromosome.
solution.why_others_wrong: Very long DNA cannot be sequenced intact; overlaps can be aligned only after the fragments are sequenced; and cloning is done before sequencing, to amplify each fragment.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Molecular Basis of Inheritance', human genome project: methodologies
solution.final_answer: Option D: Total DNA isolated and broken into random fragments → fragments cloned in bacteria or yeast using BAC or YAC vectors → fragments sequenced by automated DNA sequencers → sequences arranged on the basis of overlapping regions using computer programs → sequences annotated and assigned to chromosomes

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements about the chemistry of translation are made in NCERT?

(a) Amino acids are activated in the presence of ATP and linked to their cognate tRNA (charging of tRNA).
(b) If two charged tRNAs are brought close enough, the formation of a peptide bond between them is favoured energetically.
(c) The presence of a catalyst enhances the rate of peptide bond formation.
(d) In bacteria, the 23S rRNA acts as the enzyme (ribozyme) that forms the peptide bond.
(e) Specific tRNAs read the stop codons and bring a terminal amino acid.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.concept: Charging, energetics and catalysis in translation
solution.explanation: NCERT: translation begins with the charging (aminoacylation) of tRNA, in which amino acids are activated in the presence of ATP and linked to their cognate tRNA (a). If two such charged tRNAs are brought close enough, peptide bond formation between them is favoured energetically (b), and the presence of a catalyst enhances the rate (c). In bacteria the 23S rRNA acts as the enzyme — a ribozyme (d). There are no tRNAs for the stop codons; a release factor binds there (e false).
steps: Charged tRNAs close together → bond favoured
Stop codons: release factor, no tRNA
solution.why_others_wrong: (e) is false — there are no tRNAs for stop codons — so options containing it are wrong; '(a), (b) and (d) only' leaves out the role of the catalyst (c).
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Molecular Basis of Inheritance', translation
solution.final_answer: Option A: (a), (b), (c) and (d) only

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Match List-I (observation) with List-II (conclusion drawn from it).

List-I:
A. Bacteria infected with phages grown on radioactive sulphur were not radioactive
B. Digesting the transforming extract with DNase inhibited transformation
C. ¹⁵N-DNA showed only hybrid density after one generation in ¹⁴N medium, and equal hybrid and light DNA after two generations
D. Mice injected with heat-killed S strain plus live R strain bacteria died, and live S strain bacteria were recovered from them

List-II:
I. The R strain bacteria had been transformed by a 'transforming principle' from the heat-killed S strain
II. DNA replicates semiconservatively
III. DNA is the transforming principle
IV. The viral protein did not enter the bacteria

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: Hershey and Chase: bacteria infected with phages carrying radioactive (sulphur-labelled) protein were not radioactive, so the protein did not enter the bacteria (A-IV). Avery, MacLeod and McCarty: DNase inhibited transformation, so DNA is the transforming principle (B-III). Meselson and Stahl: hybrid DNA after 20 minutes and equal hybrid and light DNA after 40 minutes showed semiconservative replication (C-II). Griffith: the R strain had been transformed by some 'transforming principle' from the heat-killed S strain (D-I).
solution.why_others_wrong: The wrong codes give the sulphur result Avery's conclusion, mix up Avery's and Meselson–Stahl's conclusions, or interchange Meselson–Stahl's and Griffith's.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Molecular Basis of Inheritance', the search for genetic material; replication: the experimental proof
solution.final_answer: Option D: A-IV, B-III, C-II, D-I

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Which of the following involve polymerisation of nucleotides in a template-independent manner, according to NCERT?

(a) Addition of adenylate residues at the 3'-end of hnRNA (tailing)
(b) Polymerisation of RNA with defined sequences by the enzyme (polynucleotide phosphorylase) used by Severo Ochoa
(c) Synthesis of RNA by DNA-dependent RNA polymerase during transcription
(d) Synthesis of DNA by DNA-dependent DNA polymerase during replication
(e) Synthesis of the discontinuous strand at the replication fork

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: NCERT: in tailing, adenylate residues (200–300) are added at the 3'-end in a template-independent manner (a). Severo Ochoa's enzyme (polynucleotide phosphorylase) was helpful in polymerising RNA with defined sequences in a template-independent manner (b). DNA-dependent RNA polymerase and DNA-dependent DNA polymerase both copy a DNA template (c, d false), and the discontinuous strand at the fork is also made on a template (e false).
solution.why_others_wrong: Transcription and replication (including the discontinuous strand) are template-dependent, so every option containing (c), (d) or (e) is wrong.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Molecular Basis of Inheritance', transcription; genetic code
solution.final_answer: Option B: (a) and (b) only

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): When E. coli grown for many generations in ¹⁵NH₄Cl medium is transferred to ¹⁴NH₄Cl medium, the DNA extracted after 20 minutes (one generation) has a hybrid, intermediate density.
Reason (R): Taylor and colleagues used radioactive thymidine to show that DNA in the chromosomes of Vicia faba also replicates semiconservatively.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: NCERT: in the Meselson and Stahl experiment, DNA extracted after one generation (20 minutes) in ¹⁴N medium had a hybrid or intermediate density, because each molecule had one old (¹⁵N) and one new (¹⁴N) strand (A true). Taylor and colleagues (1958) used radioactive thymidine in Vicia faba to show semiconservative replication in chromosomes (R true). R reports a separate experiment on a different organism; it is not the reason for the density observed in E. coli.
steps: A: one ¹⁵N + one ¹⁴N strand → hybrid density (true)
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Molecular Basis of Inheritance', replication: the experimental proof
solution.final_answer: Option B: Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Before sewage is disposed of, it is treated in sewage treatment plants (STPs) to make it less polluting. According to NCERT, this treatment is carried out by:

options.text: Heterotrophic microbes naturally present in the sewage
Autotrophic cyanobacteria added to the sewage from paddy fields
Chemical oxidising agents added at each stage of the plant
Photosynthetic algae grown on the surface of the aeration tanks

solution.concept: Who treats sewage in an STP
solution.explanation: NCERT: sewage is treated in sewage treatment plants to make it less polluting, and this treatment is carried out by heterotrophic microbes naturally present in the sewage. In the aeration tanks, for example, aerobic microbes grow into flocs and consume the organic matter, and in the anaerobic sludge digesters other bacteria digest the sludge.
steps: Done by heterotrophic microbes already present in the sewage
solution.why_others_wrong: The microbes are not added from outside and are not autotrophs: they feed on the organic matter of the sewage. NCERT describes the process as a biological (microbial) one, not chemical oxidation.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Microbes in Human Welfare', microbes in sewage treatment
solution.final_answer: Option A: Heterotrophic microbes naturally present in the sewage

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: NCERT lists the deadly diseases that antibiotics have greatly improved our capacity to treat, giving the common Indian name of some of them. The disease that NCERT calls 'kusht rog' is:

solution.concept: Antibiotics and the diseases they treat
solution.explanation: NCERT: antibiotics have greatly improved our capacity to treat deadly diseases such as plague, whooping cough (kali khansi), diphtheria (gal ghotu) and leprosy (kusht rog), which used to kill millions all over the globe.
solution.why_others_wrong: Whooping cough is 'kali khansi' and diphtheria is 'gal ghotu' in NCERT; NCERT gives no Indian name for plague.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Microbes in Human Welfare', microbes in industrial products: antibiotics
solution.final_answer: Option C: Leprosy

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Trichoderma species, which NCERT describes as effective biocontrol agents of several plant pathogens, are free-living fungi that are very common in:

solution.explanation: NCERT: Trichoderma species are free-living fungi that are very common in the root ecosystems; they are effective biocontrol agents of several plant pathogens.
steps: Common in root ecosystems; controls plant pathogens
solution.why_others_wrong: The rumen of cattle and sludge digesters are where NCERT places methanogenic bacteria; the gut of insect larvae is where the Bt toxin is released.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Microbes in Human Welfare', microbes as biocontrol agents
solution.final_answer: Option D: Root ecosystems

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Rhizobium, Azotobacter and Anabaena are all named by NCERT as biofertilisers, while Glomus is named as a biofertiliser of a different kind. Which feature do the first three share that NCERT does NOT give for Glomus?

options.text: They live in symbiotic association with plant roots
They are autotrophs that add organic matter to the soil
They absorb phosphorus from the soil and pass it to the plant

solution.explanation: NCERT: Rhizobium fixes atmospheric nitrogen in the root nodules of legumes; Azospirillum and Azotobacter fix atmospheric nitrogen while free-living in the soil; cyanobacteria such as Anabaena, Nostoc and Oscillatoria fix atmospheric nitrogen. Glomus forms mycorrhiza, a symbiosis in which the fungus absorbs phosphorus from the soil and passes it to the plant; NCERT does not describe it as fixing nitrogen.
solution.why_others_wrong: Symbiosis with roots applies to Rhizobium and Glomus but not to free-living Azotobacter or Anabaena; only the cyanobacteria are autotrophs that add organic matter; phosphorus absorption is Glomus's own role.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Microbes in Human Welfare', microbes as biofertilisers
solution.final_answer: Option B: They fix atmospheric nitrogen

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): In a biogas plant fed with a slurry of dung, the floating cover placed over the slurry keeps on rising.
Reason (R): Gas is produced in the tank by microbial activity on the slurry.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: NCERT: the biogas plant consists of a concrete tank (10–15 feet deep) in which bio-wastes are collected and a slurry of dung is fed. A floating cover is placed over the slurry, which keeps on rising as the gas is produced in the tank due to microbial activity. The rising of the cover (A) is caused by the gas produced (R).
steps: Gas collects under the floating cover and pushes it up
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Microbes in Human Welfare', microbes in production of biogas

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Depending on the type of raw material used for fermentation and the type of processing (with or without distillation), different types of alcoholic drinks are obtained.
Statement II: The yeast used for bread-making and the brewer's yeast used for producing ethanol from malted cereals and fruit juices are two different species of Saccharomyces.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: NCERT: Saccharomyces cerevisiae, used for bread-making and commonly called brewer's yeast, is used for fermenting malted cereals and fruit juices to produce ethanol; depending on the raw material and the type of processing (with or without distillation), different types of alcoholic drinks are obtained (Statement I true). The same species serves both purposes, so Statement II is false.
steps: Drink type depends on raw material + processing
Baker's and brewer's yeast: both Saccharomyces cerevisiae

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: NCERT: microbes are diverse — protozoa, bacteria, fungi and microscopic animal and plant viruses, viroids and also prions that are proteinaceous infectious agents (Statement II true). Microbes like bacteria and fungi can be grown on nutritive media to form colonies that can be seen with the naked eyes, so Statement I is false.
steps: Colonies: visible to the naked eye
Microbes include viruses, viroids and prions

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Which of the following pairs consists of a product obtained from a BACTERIUM followed by a product obtained from a FUNGUS, according to NCERT?

solution.explanation: NCERT: butyric acid is produced by the bacterium Clostridium butylicum, and citric acid by the fungus Aspergillus niger. Acetic acid comes from the bacterium Acetobacter aceti, lactic acid from Lactobacillus (a bacterium), streptokinase from the bacterium Streptococcus, and penicillin from the mould Penicillium notatum.
solution.why_others_wrong: 'Citric acid; acetic acid' and 'penicillin; streptokinase' are fungus-then-bacterium, the reverse order; lactic acid and acetic acid both come from bacteria.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
A farmer in an ecologically sensitive area grows cabbage (a brassica). The crop has butterfly caterpillars and aphids, and the soil has several fungal plant pathogens. The farmer wants to avoid chemical pesticides and to spare the other insects of the field. Which of the following choices are supported by NCERT?

(a) Spraying a suspension of Bacillus thuringiensis spores to kill the caterpillars
(b) Encouraging ladybird beetles to get rid of the aphids
(c) Using Trichoderma species against the plant pathogens
(d) Encouraging dragonflies, which NCERT names as the main control of aphids
(e) Spraying a broad-spectrum insecticide, since it kills the caterpillars and aphids together

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: NCERT: Bt spores sprayed on brassicas kill butterfly caterpillars but leave other insects unharmed (a). The ladybird beetle is useful to get rid of aphids (b), and dragonflies are useful to get rid of mosquitoes, not aphids (d false). Trichoderma species are effective biocontrol agents of several plant pathogens (c). Broad-spectrum chemicals are toxic, kill useful as well as harmful insects and pollute the environment, so they defeat the farmer's aim (e false).
solution.why_others_wrong: Dragonflies control mosquitoes, not aphids (d), and a broad-spectrum insecticide is the opposite of the biocontrol approach (e), so every option containing (d) or (e) is wrong.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, 'Microbes in Human Welfare', microbes as biocontrol agents
solution.final_answer: Option C: (a), (b) and (c) only

Reason (R): Lipases are used in detergent formulations and are helpful in removing oily stains from the laundry.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
