solution.explanation: NCERT: ovaries are the primary female sex organs that produce the female gamete (ovum) and several steroid hormones. Primary sex organs (gonads) are the organs that produce the gametes and sex hormones, so the fact stated in R is exactly why the ovaries are called the primary female sex organs.
steps: R: true - the ovaries form the gamete and the ovarian hormones
solution.why_others_wrong: Both statements are NCERT's own; R gives the very function (gamete and hormone production) that makes the ovaries the primary sex organs, so 'R is not the explanation' is wrong, and neither statement is false.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 2 'Human Reproduction', The Female Reproductive System
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: The enlarged end of the penis, called the glans penis, is covered by a loose fold of skin called the foreskin.
Statement II: The seminal vesicles are paired, whereas the prostate is a single gland.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: NCERT: the enlarged end of the penis called the glans penis is covered by a loose fold of skin called foreskin. The male accessory glands include paired seminal vesicles, a prostate and paired bulbourethral glands. Both statements are true.
steps: Statement II: true - paired seminal vesicles, a (single) prostate
solution.why_others_wrong: Statement I is NCERT's description of the glans penis; Statement II matches NCERT's list of accessory glands (paired seminal vesicles, a prostate, paired bulbourethral glands), so no option with a false statement is correct.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 2 'Human Reproduction', The Male Reproductive System
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: In the seminiferous tubules of the human testis, some of the spermatogonia periodically undergo meiosis. These cells are called:

solution.explanation: NCERT: spermatogonia multiply by mitotic division. Some of the spermatogonia, called primary spermatocytes, periodically undergo meiosis. A primary spermatocyte completes the first meiotic division (reduction division) leading to the formation of two equal, haploid cells called secondary spermatocytes.
steps: Spermatogonia that enter meiosis = primary spermatocytes
solution.why_others_wrong: Spermatids are formed after the second meiotic division and do not divide again; Sertoli cells are nourishing cells, not germ cells; secondary spermatocytes are the products of the first meiotic division.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 2 'Human Reproduction', Gametogenesis
solution.final_answer: Option B: Primary spermatocytes

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: The glandular tissue of each human breast is divided into mammary lobes containing clusters of cells called alveoli. According to NCERT, the number of mammary lobes in each breast is:

solution.explanation: NCERT: the glandular tissue of each breast is divided into 15-20 mammary lobes containing clusters of cells called alveoli. The cells of the alveoli secrete milk, which is stored in the cavities (lumens) of the alveoli.
solution.why_others_wrong: About 250 is the number of testicular lobules in each testis; 2-3 and 60-80 are not NCERT figures for the mammary gland.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 2 'Human Reproduction', The Female Reproductive System
solution.final_answer: Option D: 15-20

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Which of the following structures of the human female reproductive system are paired?

(a) Ovaries
(b) Uterus
(c) Oviducts (fallopian tubes)
(d) Mammary glands
(e) Vagina

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.concept: Paired and single female reproductive structures
solution.explanation: NCERT: the female reproductive system consists of a pair of ovaries along with a pair of oviducts, uterus, cervix, vagina and the external genitalia, together with a pair of mammary glands. The uterus is single (also called the womb), and there is a single vagina into which the uterus opens through the cervix.
solution.why_others_wrong: '(a) and (c) only' leaves out the pair of mammary glands; options containing (b) or (e) are wrong because the uterus is single and so is the vagina.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 2 'Human Reproduction', The Female Reproductive System
solution.final_answer: Option B: (a), (c) and (d) only

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Match List-I (hormone) with List-II (cells or organ it acts on, as described in NCERT).

List-I:
A. GnRH
B. LH (in the male)
C. FSH (in the male)
D. Oxytocin (at parturition)

List-II:
I. Sertoli cells
II. Uterine muscle
III. Anterior pituitary
IV. Leydig cells

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: NCERT: at puberty the increased GnRH acts at the anterior pituitary and stimulates the secretion of two gonadotropins, LH and FSH. LH acts at the Leydig cells and stimulates the synthesis and secretion of androgens; FSH acts on the Sertoli cells and stimulates the secretion of some factors that help in spermiogenesis. At parturition, oxytocin acts on the uterine muscle and causes stronger uterine contractions.
solution.why_others_wrong: Swapping LH and FSH reverses NCERT's pairing (LH -> Leydig cells, FSH -> Sertoli cells); GnRH acts on the anterior pituitary, not on the uterus; the last code mismatches every hormone.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 2 'Human Reproduction', Gametogenesis; Parturition and Lactation
solution.final_answer: Option C: A-III, B-IV, C-I, D-II

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Using the lengths given in NCERT, which option arranges the following human structures in DECREASING order of length?

Oviduct, testis, ovary

solution.explanation: NCERT: each oviduct is about 10-12 cm long; each adult testis is about 4 to 5 cm long (2 to 3 cm wide); each ovary is about 2 to 4 cm in length. So the oviduct is the longest and the ovary the shortest.
solution.why_others_wrong: The testis (4-5 cm) is far shorter than the oviduct (10-12 cm); the ovary (2-4 cm) is not longer than the testis; the last option reverses the true order.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 2 'Human Reproduction', The Male Reproductive System; The Female Reproductive System
solution.final_answer: Option A: Oviduct > testis > ovary

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: A spermatid has the same number of chromosomes as the secondary spermatocyte from which it is formed.
Statement II: During spermiogenesis, the chromosome number of a spermatid is halved to form a spermatozoon.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.concept: Chromosome number in the later stages of spermatogenesis
solution.explanation: NCERT: secondary spermatocytes have only 23 chromosomes each. They undergo the second meiotic division to produce four equal, haploid spermatids, which also have 23 chromosomes. Spermatids are then transformed into spermatozoa (sperms) by spermiogenesis, a transformation without any further reduction, so the sperm remains haploid with 23 chromosomes.
steps: Spermiogenesis does not halve the number -> Statement II false
solution.why_others_wrong: Statement II is false because the sperm is haploid like the spermatid (23 chromosomes), so 'both true' and 'Statement I false but II true' are wrong; Statement I is true, so 'both false' is wrong.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 2 'Human Reproduction', Gametogenesis
solution.final_answer: Option C: Statement I is true but Statement II is false.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): The human sperm and the human ovum contribute equal numbers of chromosomes to the zygote.
Reason (R): Both the sperm and the ovum are haploid, and their haploid nuclei fuse to form a diploid zygote.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.concept: Contribution of gametes to the zygote
solution.explanation: NCERT: the sperm head contains an elongated haploid nucleus, and the ovum (ootid) formed after the second meiotic division is haploid. Fusion of the haploid nuclei of the sperm and the ovum forms a diploid zygote. Since each gamete is haploid (23 chromosomes), each contributes the same number, which is exactly what A says.
solution.why_others_wrong: Both statements are true, and the haploid nature of both gametes is the direct reason they contribute equal chromosome numbers; so 'R is not the explanation' and the options calling either statement false are wrong.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 2 'Human Reproduction', Fertilisation and Implantation
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
How many of the following cells of the human testis are present INSIDE the seminiferous tubules?

Spermatogonia, Sertoli cells, Leydig cells, primary spermatocytes, spermatids, immunologically competent cells

solution.concept: Inside versus outside the seminiferous tubules
solution.explanation: NCERT: each seminiferous tubule is lined on its inside by male germ cells (spermatogonia) and Sertoli cells, and spermatogenesis (primary spermatocytes -> secondary spermatocytes -> spermatids -> sperms) takes place in the tubules. The interstitial spaces outside the tubules contain small blood vessels, interstitial (Leydig) cells and some immunologically competent cells.
steps: Inside: spermatogonia, Sertoli cells, primary spermatocytes, spermatids = 4
Outside (interstitial spaces): Leydig cells, immunologically competent cells
solution.why_others_wrong: Three leaves out one of the cells of the tubule (often the Sertoli cells or the spermatids); five or six add the Leydig cells and/or the immunologically competent cells, which NCERT places in the interstitial spaces.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 2 'Human Reproduction', The Male Reproductive System; Gametogenesis
solution.final_answer: Option D: Four

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Match List-I (event) with List-II (when it takes place).

List-I:
A. Formation of oogonia (gamete mother cells) in the ovary
B. Start of spermatogenesis
C. Completion of the second meiotic division of the secondary oocyte
D. Cessation of menstrual cycles

List-II:
I. Around 50 years of age
II. During embryonic (fetal) development
III. At puberty
IV. On entry of a sperm into the oocyte

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: NCERT: oogenesis is initiated during embryonic development, when a couple of million oogonia are formed within each fetal ovary; no more oogonia are formed after birth. Spermatogenesis starts at puberty. The entry of the sperm into the ovum induces completion of the meiotic division of the secondary oocyte. In human beings, menstrual cycles cease around 50 years of age (menopause).
solution.why_others_wrong: Oogonia are formed before birth while spermatogenesis begins at puberty, so swapping A and B is wrong; the second meiotic division is completed on sperm entry, not at 50 years; the last code puts oogonia formation at sperm entry.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 2 'Human Reproduction', Gametogenesis; Menstrual Cycle; Fertilisation and Implantation
solution.final_answer: Option B: A-II, B-III, C-IV, D-I

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: The human embryo with 8 to 16 blastomeres is called a blastocyst.
Statement II: In the blastocyst, the blastomeres are arranged into an outer layer called the trophoblast and an inner group of cells attached to it called the inner cell mass.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: NCERT: the embryo with 8 to 16 blastomeres is called a morula. The morula continues to divide and transforms into a blastocyst, in which the blastomeres are arranged into an outer layer called trophoblast and an inner group of cells attached to the trophoblast called the inner cell mass.
solution.why_others_wrong: Statement I names the wrong stage (it is the morula), so options calling it true are wrong; Statement II is NCERT's description of the blastocyst, so 'both false' is wrong.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 2 'Human Reproduction', Fertilisation and Implantation
solution.final_answer: Option D: Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): In the human male, the sperms released from the seminiferous tubules are transported to the outside by the accessory ducts.
Reason (R): The secretions of the bulbourethral glands help in the lubrication of the penis.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: NCERT: the male sex accessory ducts (rete testis, vasa efferentia, epididymis and vas deferens) store and transport the sperms from the testis to the outside through the urethra; the sperms released from the seminiferous tubules are transported by these ducts. Separately, NCERT states that the secretions of the bulbourethral glands help in the lubrication of the penis. Both are true, but lubrication of the penis has nothing to do with how sperms are carried out of the testis.
steps: R describes a different structure and function -> not the explanation
solution.why_others_wrong: R concerns lubrication of the penis by a gland, while A concerns sperm transport by ducts, so R cannot explain A; both statements are NCERT's own, so the options calling either one false are wrong.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 2 'Human Reproduction', The Male Reproductive System; Gametogenesis
solution.final_answer: Option B: Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: In a human male, a group of primary spermatocytes completes spermatogenesis and forms exactly 100 spermatozoa. In a human female, a group of primary oocytes completes oogenesis and forms exactly 100 ova; assume that every secondary oocyte is entered by a sperm and completes its second meiotic division, and that the first polar bodies do not divide. Counting each splitting of one cell into two as one division, how many meiotic divisions take place in all in the male and in the female, respectively?

solution.concept: Counting meiotic divisions in spermatogenesis and oogenesis
solution.explanation: One primary spermatocyte undergoes one first meiotic division (giving two secondary spermatocytes) and then each secondary spermatocyte undergoes one second meiotic division: 3 divisions give 4 spermatids, i.e. 4 sperms. One primary oocyte undergoes the unequal first meiotic division (secondary oocyte + first polar body); only the secondary oocyte undergoes the second meiotic division (ovum + second polar body): 2 divisions give 1 ovum.
solution.why_others_wrong: '50 and 100' counts only one division per two gametes or per gamete, ignoring a meiotic step; '100 and 200' counts one division per sperm; '75 and 300' wrongly makes the first polar body divide, which the stem excludes.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 2 'Human Reproduction', Gametogenesis
solution.final_answer: Option C: 75 and 200

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Which option arranges the following events of human foetal development in the correct order, from EARLIEST to LATEST, according to NCERT?

(P) Eye-lids separate and eyelashes are formed
(Q) The heart is formed
(R) First movements of the foetus are usually observed
(S) Most of the major organ systems are formed, with the limbs and external genital organs well developed
(T) The foetus develops limbs and digits

solution.explanation: NCERT: after one month of pregnancy the embryo's heart is formed (Q). By the end of the second month the foetus develops limbs and digits (T). By the end of 12 weeks (first trimester), most major organ systems are formed, the limbs and external genital organs being well developed (S). The first movements of the foetus and appearance of hair on the head are usually observed during the fifth month (R). By the end of about 24 weeks, the body is covered with fine hair, eye-lids separate and eyelashes are formed (P).
steps: Order: Q -> T -> S -> R -> P
solution.why_others_wrong: Limbs and digits (end of month 2) come before the first trimester ends (12 weeks), so S cannot precede T; the heart forms before the limbs; first movements (fifth month) come after 12 weeks and before 24 weeks, so R can neither precede S nor follow P.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 2 'Human Reproduction', Pregnancy and Embryonic Development
solution.final_answer: Option D: Q -> T -> S -> R -> P

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
How many of the following normally take place in the human UTERUS?

Fertilisation; implantation; start of cleavage of the zygote; formation of the placenta; completion of the second meiotic division of the secondary oocyte; breakdown of the endometrial lining in the menstrual phase

solution.explanation: NCERT: fertilisation takes place in the ampullary region of the oviduct, and the second meiotic division of the secondary oocyte is completed there when the sperm enters it. Cleavage starts as the zygote moves through the isthmus of the oviduct towards the uterus. The blastocyst becomes embedded in the endometrium of the uterus (implantation); the chorionic villi and uterine tissue jointly form the placenta; in the menstrual phase the endometrial lining of the uterus breaks down.
steps: In the uterus: implantation, placenta formation, endometrial breakdown = 3
In the oviduct: fertilisation, completion of meiosis II, start of cleavage
solution.why_others_wrong: Two omits either placenta formation or menstrual breakdown; four or five add events that NCERT places in the oviduct (fertilisation, completion of meiosis II, start of cleavage).
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 2 'Human Reproduction', Fertilisation and Implantation; Pregnancy and Embryonic Development; Menstrual Cycle
solution.final_answer: Option B: Three

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): The first polar body and the secondary oocyte formed from a human primary oocyte have the same number of chromosomes.
Reason (R): The first meiotic division of the primary oocyte divides its cytoplasm equally between the two cells formed.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.concept: Unequal first meiotic division of the oocyte
solution.explanation: NCERT: the primary oocyte completes its first meiotic division, an unequal division, resulting in a large haploid secondary oocyte and a tiny first polar body; the secondary oocyte retains the bulk of the nutrient-rich cytoplasm. Both cells are haploid (23 chromosomes each), so A is true; the cytoplasm is divided unequally, so R is false.
steps: Both cells haploid -> same chromosome number -> A true
solution.why_others_wrong: The division is unequal in cytoplasm but equal in chromosomes; so R is false and the two 'both true' options fail, and A is true so 'A is false but R is true' fails.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 2 'Human Reproduction', Gametogenesis
solution.final_answer: Option C: A is true but R is false.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: In a menstrual cycle, the LH surge takes place before the corpus luteum is formed.
Statement II: Progesterone secreted by the corpus luteum causes the rupture of the Graafian follicle at ovulation.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.concept: Sequence of hormonal events around ovulation
solution.explanation: NCERT: the rapid secretion of LH reaching a maximum in the middle of the cycle (LH surge) induces rupture of the Graafian follicle and thereby the release of the ovum (ovulation). The ovulatory phase is followed by the luteal phase, during which the remaining parts of the Graafian follicle transform into the corpus luteum, which then secretes large amounts of progesterone. So the LH surge comes before the corpus luteum (I true), and ovulation is caused by the LH surge, not by progesterone, which comes only from the corpus luteum formed after ovulation (II false).
steps: LH surge -> ovulation -> corpus luteum -> progesterone
solution.why_others_wrong: Statement II reverses cause and sequence: the corpus luteum (the source of progesterone) forms only after the follicle has ruptured, so options calling it true fail; Statement I is true, so 'both false' and 'Statement I false' fail.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 2 'Human Reproduction', Menstrual Cycle
solution.final_answer: Option C: Statement I is true but Statement II is false.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Match List-I (cell) with List-II (description).

List-I:
A. Spermatogonium
B. Secondary spermatocyte
C. Primary oocyte in the fetal ovary
D. First polar body

List-II:
I. Haploid; tiny cell formed by an unequal meiotic division
II. Diploid; temporarily arrested in prophase-I of meiosis
III. Diploid; increases in number by mitotic division
IV. Haploid; undergoes the second meiotic division to form two equal cells

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.concept: Ploidy and fate of gametogenic cells
solution.explanation: NCERT: spermatogonia are diploid (46 chromosomes) and multiply by mitotic division. A primary spermatocyte completes the first meiotic division to form two equal haploid secondary spermatocytes, which undergo the second meiotic division to produce four equal haploid spermatids. In the fetal ovary, the oogonia enter prophase-I of meiosis and get temporarily arrested as (diploid) primary oocytes. The primary oocyte's unequal first meiotic division forms a large secondary oocyte and a tiny first polar body.
solution.why_others_wrong: It is the primary oocyte, not the spermatogonium, that is arrested in prophase-I; the secondary spermatocyte divides into two equal cells, whereas the first polar body is the tiny product of an unequal division; the last code makes the diploid spermatogonium haploid.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 2 'Human Reproduction', Gametogenesis
solution.final_answer: Option A: A-III, B-IV, C-II, D-I

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Which of the following are induced by a sperm when it contacts or enters the human secondary oocyte during fertilisation?

(a) Changes in the membrane of the ovum that block the entry of additional sperms
(b) Completion of the meiotic division of the secondary oocyte
(c) Completion of the first meiotic division of the primary oocyte
(d) Formation of the second polar body
(e) Rupture of the Graafian follicle

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: NCERT: during fertilisation a sperm comes in contact with the zona pellucida layer of the ovum and induces changes in the membrane that block the entry of additional sperms. The entry of the sperm into the ovum induces completion of the meiotic division of the secondary oocyte; this second meiotic division is unequal and forms the second polar body and a haploid ovum. The first meiotic division is completed in the tertiary follicle before ovulation, and the Graafian follicle ruptures under the LH surge.
steps: (c) before ovulation; (e) LH surge -> not induced by the sperm
solution.why_others_wrong: '(b) and (d) only' omits the block to additional sperms, which NCERT says the sperm's contact induces; (c) occurs before ovulation and (e) is caused by the LH surge, so options containing them are wrong.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 2 'Human Reproduction', Fertilisation and Implantation; Gametogenesis
solution.final_answer: Option D: (a), (b) and (d) only

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: According to NCERT, the Government of India legalised medical termination of pregnancy (MTP), with some strict conditions to avoid its misuse, in the year:

solution.explanation: NCERT: the Government of India legalised MTP in 1971 with some strict conditions to avoid its misuse. Such restrictions are all the more important to check indiscriminate and illegal female foeticides.
solution.why_others_wrong: 1951 is the year in which the 'family planning' programmes were initiated in India; 1991 and 2011 are not the year NCERT gives for legalising MTP.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 3 'Reproductive Health', Medical Termination of Pregnancy (MTP)
solution.final_answer: Option A: 1971

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: Which of the following groups consists ONLY of barrier methods of contraception?

options.text: Condoms, diaphragms, Lippes loop and vaults
Condoms, diaphragms, cervical caps and vaults
Cervical caps, vaults, Saheli and condoms
Diaphragms, CuT, cervical caps and coitus interruptus

solution.explanation: NCERT: in barrier methods, ovum and sperms are prevented from physically meeting with the help of barriers. Such methods are available for both males and females: condoms, and diaphragms, cervical caps and vaults made of rubber that are inserted into the female reproductive tract to cover the cervix during coitus.
steps: Barriers: condoms, diaphragms, cervical caps, vaults
Not barriers: IUDs (CuT, Lippes loop), pills (Saheli), natural methods, surgical methods
solution.why_others_wrong: Lippes loop and CuT are intra-uterine devices, Saheli is an oral pill, and coitus interruptus is a natural method, so every other group contains a non-barrier method.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 3 'Reproductive Health', Population Stabilisation and Birth Control
solution.final_answer: Option B: Condoms, diaphragms, cervical caps and vaults

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): IUDs are ideal contraceptives for females who want to delay pregnancy and/or space children.
Reason (R): IUDs are inserted by doctors or expert nurses in the uterus through the vagina.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: NCERT: IUDs are inserted by doctors or expert nurses in the uterus through the vagina. IUDs are ideal contraceptives for the females who want to delay pregnancy and/or space children; it is one of the most widely accepted methods of contraception in India. Both statements are true, but who inserts the device and by what route does not explain why it is suited for delaying or spacing pregnancies.
steps: R describes the insertion procedure, not the reason for suitability -> not the explanation
solution.why_others_wrong: R gives a procedural detail unrelated to the purpose described in A, so 'R is the correct explanation' is wrong; both statements are NCERT's own, so the options calling either false are wrong.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 3 'Reproductive Health', Population Stabilisation and Birth Control
solution.final_answer: Option B: Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Surgical methods of contraception are highly effective.
Statement II: In the lactational amenorrhea method, no medicines or devices are used, and its chances of failure are almost nil.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.concept: Effectiveness of surgical and natural methods
solution.explanation: NCERT: sterilisation techniques (vasectomy, tubectomy) are highly effective, but their reversibility is very poor. Lactational amenorrhea is a natural method; for such methods NCERT says that as no medicines or devices are used, side effects are almost nil, but the chances of failure are also high. So it is the side effects, not the chances of failure, that are almost nil.
steps: Statement II: false - side effects almost nil, chances of failure high
solution.why_others_wrong: Statement II confuses side effects with failure; natural methods have high chances of failure, so options calling it true are wrong. Statement I is NCERT's own statement, so 'both false' and 'Statement I false' are wrong.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 3 'Reproductive Health', Population Stabilisation and Birth Control
solution.final_answer: Option C: Statement I is true but Statement II is false.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: LNG-20 is an example of a:

options.text: Barrier device that covers the cervix

solution.explanation: NCERT classifies IUDs as non-medicated IUDs (e.g. Lippes loop), copper-releasing IUDs (CuT, Cu7, Multiload 375) and hormone-releasing IUDs (Progestasert, LNG-20).
solution.why_others_wrong: Copper-releasing IUDs are CuT, Cu7 and Multiload 375; the non-medicated IUD named by NCERT is Lippes loop; the barriers covering the cervix are diaphragms, cervical caps and vaults.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 3 'Reproductive Health', Population Stabilisation and Birth Control
solution.final_answer: Option D: Hormone-releasing IUD

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
How many of the following are intra-uterine devices (IUDs)?

Lippes loop, CuT, Saheli, LNG-20, Multiload 375, vault, Progestasert

solution.explanation: NCERT's IUDs: non-medicated (Lippes loop), copper-releasing (CuT, Cu7, Multiload 375) and hormone-releasing (Progestasert, LNG-20). Saheli is an oral contraceptive pill, and the vault is a rubber barrier that covers the cervix.
steps: IUDs: Lippes loop, CuT, LNG-20, Multiload 375, Progestasert = 5
solution.why_others_wrong: Three or four leave out one or more of NCERT's IUDs (often the hormone-releasing ones); six counts the vault or Saheli, which are a barrier and a pill.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 3 'Reproductive Health', Population Stabilisation and Birth Control
solution.final_answer: Option C: Five

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Progestogens, progestogen-estrogen combinations or IUDs can be used to avoid a possible pregnancy following rape or casual unprotected intercourse.
Reason (R): Such emergency contraceptives are very effective only if used within 24 hours of coitus.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: NCERT: administration of progestogens or progestogen-estrogen combinations or IUDs within 72 hours of coitus has been found to be very effective as emergency contraceptives, as they could be used to avoid possible pregnancy due to rape or casual unprotected intercourse. A is true; R gives the wrong time limit (24 hours instead of 72 hours), so R is false.
steps: R: false - NCERT's window is 72 hours
solution.why_others_wrong: R changes NCERT's 72-hour window to 24 hours, so options with R true are wrong; A is NCERT's own statement, so 'A is false' is wrong.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 3 'Reproductive Health', Population Stabilisation and Birth Control
solution.final_answer: Option C: A is true but R is false.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
According to NCERT, educating people, especially fertile couples and those in the marriageable age group, about which of the following would help in bringing up socially conscious healthy families of desired size?

(a) Available birth control options
(b) Care of pregnant mothers and post-natal care of the mother and child
(c) Importance of breast feeding
(d) Equal opportunities for the male and the female child
(e) Methods of finding out the sex of the foetus

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.concept: Reproductive health strategies: education of couples
solution.explanation: NCERT: educating people, especially fertile couples and those in the marriageable age group, about available birth control options, care of pregnant mothers, post-natal care of the mother and child, importance of breast feeding, equal opportunities for the male and the female child, etc., would address the importance of bringing up socially conscious healthy families of desired size. Foetal sex determination is not among these; NCERT describes a statutory ban on amniocentesis for sex determination.
steps: (e): not listed - sex determination of the foetus is banned
solution.why_others_wrong: The shorter options leave out equal opportunities for the male and female child and/or the importance of breast feeding, both named by NCERT; the option with (e) includes foetal sex determination, which is legally banned and not part of this education.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 3 'Reproductive Health', Reproductive Health - Problems and Strategies
solution.final_answer: Option D: (a), (b), (c) and (d) only

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Match List-I (strategy for reproductive health described in NCERT) with List-II (what it is meant to achieve).

List-I:
A. Proper information about reproductive organs, adolescence and related changes, safe and hygienic sexual practices, STIs and AIDS
B. Awareness of problems due to uncontrolled population growth and of social evils like sex-abuse and sex-related crimes
C. Strong infrastructural facilities, professional expertise and material support
D. Implementation of better techniques and new strategies from time to time

List-II:
I. To provide more efficient care and assistance to people
II. To help people, especially those in the adolescent age group, lead a reproductively healthy life
III. To provide medical assistance and care in problems like pregnancy, delivery, STDs, abortions, contraception, menstrual problems and infertility
IV. To enable people to take steps to prevent them and build a socially responsible and healthy society

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: NCERT (Reproductive Health - Problems and Strategies): proper information about reproductive organs, adolescence and related changes, safe and hygienic sexual practices, STIs, AIDS, etc., would help people, especially those in the adolescent age group, to lead a reproductively healthy life. Awareness of problems due to uncontrolled population growth and social evils like sex-abuse and sex-related crimes needs to be created to enable people to take up necessary steps to prevent them and build a socially responsible and healthy society. Strong infrastructural facilities, professional expertise and material support are essential to provide medical assistance and care in reproduction-related problems like pregnancy, delivery, STDs, abortions, contraception, menstrual problems and infertility. Better techniques and new strategies from time to time are required to provide more efficient care and assistance.
solution.why_others_wrong: Information on reproductive organs and safe practices is aimed at adolescents, while awareness of population growth and sex-related crimes is aimed at building a responsible society, so swapping A and B is wrong; infrastructure and expertise provide medical care, whereas new techniques make care more efficient, so swapping C and D is wrong; the last code mismatches every row.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 3 'Reproductive Health', Reproductive Health - Problems and Strategies
solution.final_answer: Option A: A-II, B-IV, C-III, D-I

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: According to NCERT, a society whose people have physically and functionally normal reproductive organs can be called reproductively healthy, even if emotional and behavioural interactions in sex-related aspects are not normal.
Statement II: Creating awareness among people about various reproduction-related aspects and providing facilities and support for building up a reproductively healthy society are the major tasks under the Reproductive and Child Health Care (RCH) programmes.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.concept: Meaning of a reproductively healthy society
solution.explanation: NCERT: a society with people having physically and functionally normal reproductive organs AND normal emotional and behavioural interactions among them in all sex-related aspects might be called reproductively healthy; reproductive health means total well-being in all aspects of reproduction, i.e. physical, emotional, behavioural and social. Creating awareness about reproduction-related aspects and providing facilities and support for building up a reproductively healthy society are the major tasks under the RCH programmes.
steps: Statement I: false - emotional and behavioural interactions must also be normal
solution.why_others_wrong: Statement I drops the emotional and behavioural part of NCERT's description, so options calling it true are wrong; Statement II is NCERT's own description of the RCH programmes, so 'both false' is wrong.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 3 'Reproductive Health', Reproductive Health - Problems and Strategies
solution.final_answer: Option D: Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: Which of the following correctly distinguishes vasectomy from tubectomy?

options.text: In vasectomy the vas deferens is cut or tied through an incision in the abdomen; in tubectomy the fallopian tube is cut or tied through an incision on the scrotum
In vasectomy the vas deferens is cut or tied through an incision on the scrotum; in tubectomy the fallopian tube is cut or tied through an incision in the abdomen or through the vagina
Vasectomy is easily reversible, whereas tubectomy is a terminal method
Vasectomy stops the production of sperms, whereas tubectomy stops ovulation

solution.explanation: NCERT: in vasectomy, a small part of the vas deferens is removed or tied up through a small incision on the scrotum, whereas in tubectomy, a small part of the fallopian tube is removed or tied up through a small incision in the abdomen or through the vagina. Both are sterilisation (terminal) methods that block gamete transport; their reversibility is very poor.
steps: Vasectomy: vas deferens, incision on the scrotum
Tubectomy: fallopian tube, incision in the abdomen or via the vagina
solution.why_others_wrong: The first wrong option swaps the incision sites (the scrotum belongs to the male); both methods have very poor reversibility; neither stops gamete formation, they only block gamete transport.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 3 'Reproductive Health', Population Stabilisation and Birth Control
solution.final_answer: Option B: In vasectomy the vas deferens is cut or tied through an incision on the scrotum; in tubectomy the fallopian tube is cut or tied through an incision in the abdomen or through the vagina

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Match List-I (contraceptive method) with List-II (step of reproduction it prevents).

List-I:
A. Coitus interruptus
B. Lactational amenorrhea
C. Vasectomy
D. Condom

List-II:
I. Ovulation
II. Transport of sperms from the testes through the vas deferens
III. Ejaculated semen entering the female reproductive tract, by a thin rubber/latex sheath
IV. Deposition of semen in the vagina, by withdrawal of the penis just before ejaculation

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: NCERT: in coitus interruptus the male partner withdraws his penis from the vagina just before ejaculation so as to avoid insemination. Lactational amenorrhea is based on the fact that ovulation and therefore the cycle do not occur during the period of intense lactation. In vasectomy a small part of the vas deferens is removed or tied up, blocking sperm transport. Condoms are barriers made of thin rubber/latex sheath that prevent the ejaculated semen from entering the female reproductive tract.
solution.why_others_wrong: Coitus interruptus uses no sheath (it is withdrawal), so swapping A and D is wrong; lactational amenorrhea acts on ovulation, not on the vas deferens; the last code mismatches every method.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 3 'Reproductive Health', Population Stabilisation and Birth Control
solution.final_answer: Option D: A-IV, B-I, C-II, D-III

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: Two intra-uterine devices are named below as a pair (first; second). The FIRST is an IUD that releases no substance and acts only by increasing the phagocytosis of sperms within the uterus; the SECOND, in addition, releases ions that suppress sperm motility and the fertilising capacity of sperms. Which pair fits this description?

solution.explanation: NCERT: IUDs increase phagocytosis of sperms within the uterus, and the Cu ions released from copper-releasing IUDs suppress sperm motility and the fertilising capacity of sperms. Lippes loop is a non-medicated IUD; CuT, Cu7 and Multiload 375 are copper-releasing IUDs; Progestasert and LNG-20 are hormone-releasing IUDs.
solution.why_others_wrong: Reversing the pair makes the copper IUD the one that releases nothing; Progestasert releases a hormone, so it cannot be the IUD that releases no substance, nor the one that releases copper ions.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 3 'Reproductive Health', Population Stabilisation and Birth Control
solution.final_answer: Option A: Lippes loop; Multiload 375

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Which of the following contraceptive methods act, at least in part, at the level of the CERVIX, according to NCERT's description of how they work?

(a) Cervical cap
(b) Diaphragm
(c) Hormone-releasing IUD
(d) Oral contraceptive pills
(e) Vasectomy

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: NCERT: diaphragms, cervical caps and vaults are inserted into the female reproductive tract to cover the cervix during coitus. Hormone-releasing IUDs make the uterus unsuitable for implantation and the cervix hostile to the sperms. Oral pills inhibit ovulation and implantation and also alter the quality of cervical mucus to prevent or retard the entry of sperms. Vasectomy acts on the vas deferens of the male.
solution.why_others_wrong: Stopping at the barriers misses the hormonal IUD (hostile cervix) and/or the pills (cervical mucus); vasectomy acts in the male duct system, so any option with (e) is wrong.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 3 'Reproductive Health', Population Stabilisation and Birth Control
solution.final_answer: Option B: (a), (b), (c) and (d) only

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Among the assisted reproductive technologies described in NCERT, GIFT is the one in which an ovum, rather than a zygote or an embryo, is transferred into the female.
Statement II: In artificial insemination, including intra-uterine insemination (IUI), fertilisation takes place inside the body of the female.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.concept: What is transferred in different ARTs
solution.explanation: NCERT: in ZIFT the zygote or early embryo (up to 8 blastomeres) is transferred into the fallopian tube, and in IUT embryos with more than 8 blastomeres are transferred into the uterus. In GIFT an ovum collected from a donor is transferred into the fallopian tube of a female who cannot produce one but can provide a suitable environment for fertilisation. ICSI forms an embryo in the laboratory. In artificial insemination, semen is introduced into the vagina or into the uterus (IUI), so the gametes fuse within the female body.
steps: GIFT: ovum transferred; ZIFT: zygote; IUT: embryo -> Statement I true
AI/IUI: semen introduced, fertilisation in vivo -> Statement II true
solution.why_others_wrong: Both statements follow from NCERT's descriptions of the techniques, so every option with a false statement is wrong.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 3 'Reproductive Health', Infertility
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
How many of the following does NCERT name as sexually transmitted infections (STIs)?

Gonorrhoea, syphilis, typhoid, genital herpes, chlamydiasis, genital warts, filariasis, trichomoniasis, hepatitis-B, HIV infection

solution.explanation: NCERT: diseases or infections transmitted through sexual intercourse are called STIs; gonorrhoea, syphilis, genital herpes, chlamydiasis, genital warts, trichomoniasis, hepatitis-B and HIV (leading to AIDS) are some of the common STIs. Typhoid (spread through contaminated food and water) and filariasis (spread by the bite of the female mosquito vector) are not STIs.
steps: STIs: gonorrhoea, syphilis, genital herpes, chlamydiasis, genital warts, trichomoniasis, hepatitis-B, HIV = 8
solution.why_others_wrong: Six or seven omit NCERT STIs such as hepatitis-B or HIV (which also spread in other ways); ten counts typhoid and filariasis, which are not sexually transmitted.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 3 'Reproductive Health', Sexually Transmitted Infections (STIs)
solution.final_answer: Option C: Eight

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: Fossils found in different-aged rock sediments are used as evidence for evolution. Which method does NCERT refer to for calculating the ages of fossils?

options.text: Comparing the similarities in proteins and genes
Counting the number of sediment layers above them
Measuring the size of the fossil

solution.explanation: NCERT: fossils are remains of hard parts of life-forms found in rocks, and different-aged rock sediments contain fossils of different life-forms. While discussing palaeontological evidence, NCERT asks the reader to recall how the ages of fossils are calculated, i.e. the method of radioactive dating and the principles behind it.
solution.why_others_wrong: Protein and gene similarities are biochemical evidence of common ancestry, not a way to date fossils; NCERT does not describe counting layers or measuring size as methods for calculating the age of fossils.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 6 'Evolution', What are the Evidences for Evolution?
solution.final_answer: Option C: Radioactive dating

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: S.L. Miller, an American scientist, created conditions similar to those of the early earth on a laboratory scale and observed the formation of amino acids. According to NCERT, he did this experiment in:

solution.explanation: NCERT: in 1953, S.L. Miller, an American scientist, created electric discharge in a closed flask containing CH4, H2, NH3 and water vapour and observed the formation of amino acids.
solution.why_others_wrong: 1938 is the year a coelacanth was caught in South Africa; 1891 is when Homo erectus fossils were found in Java; 1920 is the year of the post-industrial moth collection in England.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 6 'Evolution', Origin of Life
solution.final_answer: Option A: 1953

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: NCERT notes that man's intensive breeding programmes have created breeds that differ from other breeds but still are of the same group. Which animal does NCERT give as the example?

solution.explanation: NCERT: man has bred selected plants and animals for agriculture, horticulture, sport and security, and has domesticated many wild animals and crops. This intensive breeding programme has created breeds that differ from other breeds (e.g., dogs) but still are of the same group.
solution.why_others_wrong: Moths are NCERT's example of industrial melanism, finches of adaptive radiation in the Galapagos, and marsupials of adaptive radiation in Australia; none of these is an example of breeds made by man.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 6 'Evolution', What are the Evidences for Evolution?
solution.final_answer: Option D: Dogs

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: According to NCERT, evolution by natural selection, in a true sense, would have started when:

options.text: The first giant molecules such as RNA and proteins formed in the oceans
Cellular forms of life with differences in metabolic capability originated on earth
The first mammals appeared on land
Human beings began agriculture and settlements

solution.concept: Beginning of evolution by natural selection
solution.explanation: NCERT (Biological Evolution): evolution by natural selection, in a true sense, would have started when cellular forms of life with differences in metabolic capability originated on earth. Selection needs differences among individuals that affect survival and reproduction.
steps: Start: cellular forms of life with differences in metabolic capability
solution.why_others_wrong: NCERT links true natural selection to cellular life with metabolic differences, not to the earlier non-cellular giant molecules; mammals and agriculture came far later in the history of life.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 6 'Evolution', Biological Evolution
solution.final_answer: Option B: Cellular forms of life with differences in metabolic capability originated on earth

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: Early Greek thinkers thought that units of life called spores were transferred to different planets, including the earth. According to NCERT, this idea of 'panspermia' is still a favourite idea for:

solution.explanation: NCERT: some scientists believe that life came from outer space. Early Greek thinkers thought units of life called spores were transferred to different planets including earth. 'Panspermia' is still a favourite idea for some astronomers.
solution.why_others_wrong: Oparin and Haldane proposed chemical evolution from non-living organic molecules; Pasteur showed that life comes only from pre-existing life; NCERT says the majority accept that life arose through evolutionary forces from non-living molecules.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 6 'Evolution', Origin of Life
solution.final_answer: Option B: Some astronomers

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): In England, the collection of moths made in the 1850s had more dark-winged (melanised) moths than white-winged moths.
Reason (R): The 1850s collection of moths was made before industrialisation set in.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: NCERT: in a collection of moths made in the 1850s, i.e. before industrialisation set in, there were more white-winged moths on trees than dark-winged or melanised moths; in the collection from the same area after industrialisation (1920), there were more dark-winged moths. So A is false and R is true.
steps: A: false - the 1850s collection had more white-winged moths
solution.why_others_wrong: A reverses NCERT's observation for the 1850s, so all options calling A true are wrong; R is correct, so 'A is false but R is true' is the answer.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 6 'Evolution', What are the Evidences for Evolution?
solution.final_answer: Option D: A is false but R is true.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: A population is in Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium for a gene with two alleles, A and a. The combined frequency of the two homozygous genotypes (AA + aa) is exactly equal to the frequency of the heterozygous genotype (Aa). What is the frequency of allele a?

solution.explanation: Under Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium the genotype frequencies are p² (AA), 2pq (Aa) and q² (aa), with p + q = 1 and p² + 2pq + q² = 1. If p² + q² = 2pq, then p² - 2pq + q² = 0, i.e. (p - q)² = 0, so p = q = 0.5.
solution.shortcut: Homozygotes = heterozygotes = 0.5 each, which happens only when p = q.
solution.why_others_wrong: 0.25 is q² at p = q, not q; 0.71 comes from wrongly setting q² = 0.5; 0.33 comes from treating the three genotypes as equally frequent.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 6 'Evolution', Hardy-Weinberg Principle
solution.final_answer: Option B: 0.5

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: The flippers of penguins (birds) and of dolphins (mammals) look alike and perform the same function. According to NCERT, which of the following best explains such similarity?

options.text: A similar habitat has resulted in the selection of similar adaptive features in different groups of organisms, towards the same function
The same structure developed along different directions due to adaptations to different needs
Penguins and dolphins arose from one ancestral stock within a single adaptive radiation
The flippers were developed by use during the lives of the animals and passed on to the offspring

solution.explanation: NCERT: analogous structures are a result of convergent evolution - different structures evolving for the same function and hence having similarity; the flippers of penguins and dolphins are an example. One can say that it is the similar habitat that has resulted in selection of similar adaptive features in different groups of organisms, but towards the same function.
steps: Cause: similar habitat selects similar adaptive features
solution.why_others_wrong: Development of one structure in different directions describes homology (divergent evolution); penguins and dolphins belong to different groups and are not one adaptive radiation; inheritance of characters acquired by use is Lamarck's idea, not NCERT's explanation.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 6 'Evolution', What are the Evidences for Evolution?
solution.final_answer: Option A: A similar habitat has resulted in the selection of similar adaptive features in different groups of organisms, towards the same function

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): NCERT argues that nature could have created new types of organisms over millions of years.
Reason (R): Within hundreds of years, man has been able to create new breeds of animals and plants by intensive breeding programmes.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: NCERT: man has bred selected plants and animals and, by intensive breeding programmes, created breeds that differ from other breeds but still are of the same group. It is argued that if within hundreds of years man could create new breeds, could not nature have done the same over millions of years? The argument in A rests directly on the fact in R.
steps: R: man-made breeds within hundreds of years
A: inference - nature could do the same over millions of years
R is the basis of A -> R explains A
solution.why_others_wrong: A is drawn by NCERT from R itself, so 'R is not the explanation' is wrong; both statements are NCERT's own, so the options calling either false are wrong.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 6 'Evolution', What are the Evidences for Evolution?
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Although Mendel had talked of inheritable 'factors' influencing the phenotype, Darwin either ignored or kept silence on these aspects.
Statement II: Hugo de Vries believed that the minor heritable variations described by Darwin, rather than mutations, cause evolution.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.concept: Source of variation: Darwin and de Vries
solution.explanation: NCERT (Mechanism of Evolution): even though Mendel had talked of inheritable 'factors' influencing phenotype, Darwin either ignored or kept silence on these aspects. The work of Hugo de Vries on evening primrose brought forth the idea of mutations; he believed that it is mutation which causes evolution and not the minor (heritable) variations that Darwin talked about.
steps: Statement II: false - de Vries held the reverse
solution.why_others_wrong: Statement II reverses de Vries' view, so options calling it true are wrong; Statement I is NCERT's own line, so 'both false' and 'Statement I false' are wrong.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 6 'Evolution', Mechanism of Evolution
solution.final_answer: Option C: Statement I is true but Statement II is false.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Match List-I (term) with List-II (description given in NCERT).

List-I:
A. Darwinian variations
B. Mutations (as proposed by de Vries)
C. Evolution, as Darwin saw it
D. Saltation

List-II:
I. Single-step large mutation
II. Gradual
III. Random and directionless
IV. Small and directional

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.concept: Darwin's and de Vries' views compared
solution.explanation: NCERT: mutations are random and directionless while Darwinian variations are small and directional. Evolution for Darwin was gradual, while de Vries believed mutation caused speciation and hence called it saltation (single-step large mutation).
solution.why_others_wrong: Swapping A and B gives Darwin's variations the features of mutations; swapping C and D makes Darwin's evolution saltatory; the last code mismatches every term.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 6 'Evolution', Mechanism of Evolution
solution.final_answer: Option D: A-IV, B-III, C-II, D-I

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: The study of fossils shows that every form of life has existed throughout the whole history of the earth.
Statement II: The study of fossils shows that certain life forms are restricted to certain geological time-spans, so new forms of life have arisen at different times in the history of the earth.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: NCERT: the study of fossils in different sedimentary layers indicates the geological period in which they existed. The study showed that life-forms varied over time and certain life forms are restricted to certain geological time-spans. Hence new forms of life have arisen at different times in the history of the earth. This is palaeontological evidence.
steps: Statement I: false - life forms varied over time
solution.why_others_wrong: Statement I contradicts the fossil record described by NCERT, so options calling it true are wrong; Statement II is NCERT's conclusion, so 'both false' is wrong.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 6 'Evolution', What are the Evidences for Evolution?
solution.final_answer: Option D: Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: NCERT compares the skulls of an adult modern human being, a baby chimpanzee and an adult chimpanzee. What does this comparison show?

options.text: The skull of the adult chimpanzee is more like the adult human skull than the baby chimpanzee skull
The skulls of the baby and the adult chimpanzee are identical, and both differ from the human skull
The skull of the baby chimpanzee is more like the adult human skull than the adult chimpanzee skull
The skull of the baby chimpanzee resembles neither the adult chimpanzee skull nor the adult human skull

solution.explanation: NCERT (Origin and Evolution of Man) gives a comparison of the skulls of an adult modern human being, a baby chimpanzee and an adult chimpanzee, and notes that the skull of the baby chimpanzee is more like the adult human skull than the adult chimpanzee skull.
steps: Baby chimpanzee skull resembles the adult human skull more than the adult chimpanzee skull
solution.why_others_wrong: NCERT's point is the reverse of the first option; baby and adult chimpanzee skulls are not identical; and the baby chimpanzee skull does resemble the adult human skull.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 6 'Evolution', Origin and Evolution of Man
solution.final_answer: Option C: The skull of the baby chimpanzee is more like the adult human skull than the adult chimpanzee skull

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: In rural areas of England where industrialisation had not occurred, the count of melanic (dark-winged) moths was low.
Statement II: According to NCERT, this observation supports the belief that, in a given background, moths that did not match the background were picked out by predators.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.concept: Industrial melanism: evidence from rural areas
solution.explanation: NCERT: before industrialisation, thick growth of almost white-coloured lichen covered the trees and the white-winged moths survived while dark moths were picked out by predators; after industrialisation, the trunks became dark with smoke and the reverse happened. NCERT adds that this belief is supported by the fact that in rural areas where industrialisation had not occurred, the count of melanic moths was low.
steps: Statement II: true - NCERT uses it as support for the predation explanation
solution.why_others_wrong: Both statements are NCERT's own, so each option with a false statement is wrong.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: A population is in Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium for a gene with two alleles, A and a, and allele A is the more common one. The frequency of the AA genotype exceeds that of the aa genotype by exactly 0.20. What is the frequency of heterozygotes (Aa)?

solution.explanation: p² - q² = (p + q)(p - q). Since p + q = 1, p² - q² = p - q. So p - q = 0.20 and p + q = 1, giving p = 0.6 and q = 0.4. The heterozygote frequency is 2pq = 2 x 0.6 x 0.4 = 0.48. Check: p² = 0.36, q² = 0.16, difference 0.20.
steps: p² - q² = (p + q)(p - q) = p - q = 0.20
solution.shortcut: For two alleles, p² - q² always equals p - q.
solution.why_others_wrong: 0.42 uses p = 0.7 (taking the difference of allele frequencies as 0.4); 0.32 uses p = 0.8 (treating 0.2 as q); 0.50 assumes p = q, which would make the homozygote frequencies equal.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 6 'Evolution', Hardy-Weinberg Principle
solution.final_answer: Option C: 0.48

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements about fitness are correct according to NCERT?

(a) The so-called fitness is based on characteristics which are inherited.
(b) Adaptive ability is inherited; it has a genetic basis.
(c) Fitness is the end result of the ability to adapt and get selected by nature.
(d) According to Darwin, the fitness of an individual refers to its physical strength.
(e) Characters developed by the use of organs during an individual's life form the basis of fitness.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: NCERT: nature selects for fitness; the so-called fitness is based on characteristics which are inherited, so there must be a genetic basis for getting selected and to evolve. Some organisms are better adapted to survive in an otherwise hostile environment; adaptive ability is inherited and has a genetic basis. Fitness is the end result of the ability to adapt and get selected by nature. For Darwin, fitness ultimately and only refers to reproductive fitness. Use and disuse of organs is Lamarck's idea.
steps: (e): false - acquired characters (Lamarck), not inherited ones
solution.why_others_wrong: '(a) and (b) only' leaves out NCERT's description of fitness as the end result of adaptation and selection; fitness in Darwin's sense is reproductive, not physical strength, and fitness rests on inherited, not acquired, characters, so options with (d) or (e) are wrong.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 6 'Evolution', Biological Evolution; Evolution of Life Forms - A Theory
solution.final_answer: Option A: (a), (b) and (c) only

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: In a very large population with no migration, no new mutations and random mating, individuals of genotype aa consistently leave fewer surviving offspring than AA and Aa individuals in every generation, and the frequency of allele a falls steadily. Which of the factors that NCERT lists as affecting Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium is acting here?

solution.concept: Identifying the factor disturbing Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium
solution.explanation: NCERT lists five factors that affect Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium: gene migration (gene flow), genetic drift, mutation, genetic recombination and natural selection. Natural selection is a process in which heritable variations enabling better survival are enabled to reproduce and leave a greater number of progeny. Here a genotype consistently leaves fewer offspring - a systematic, not chance, effect - in a very large population with no migration or mutation.
steps: Very large population, consistent effect -> not chance (drift)
Differential reproduction by genotype -> natural selection
solution.why_others_wrong: Genetic drift and the founder effect are chance changes, typically in small samples, not a steady, genotype-linked difference in reproduction in a very large population; gene flow needs migration, which the stem excludes.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 6 'Evolution', Hardy-Weinberg Principle
solution.final_answer: Option B: Natural selection

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: If the allele frequencies of a population remain stable and constant from generation to generation, the population is undergoing evolution.
Statement II: A change in the frequency of alleles in a population, i.e. a disturbance of Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium, is interpreted as resulting in evolution.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: NCERT: the Hardy-Weinberg principle says that allele frequencies in a population are stable and constant from generation to generation; the gene pool remains a constant (genetic equilibrium). Disturbance in genetic equilibrium, or Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium, i.e. a change of frequency of alleles in a population, is then interpreted as resulting in evolution. Stable allele frequencies therefore mean no evolution at that gene.
steps: Statement I: false - stable frequencies = genetic equilibrium
solution.why_others_wrong: Statement I describes equilibrium as evolution, the opposite of NCERT, so options calling it true are wrong; Statement II is NCERT's interpretation, so 'both false' is wrong.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 6 'Evolution', Hardy-Weinberg Principle
solution.final_answer: Option D: Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: For a gene with two alleles, A (frequency p) and a (frequency q), in a population in Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium, which of the following is ALWAYS true, whatever the value of p?

options.text: The frequency of genotype AA is always greater than that of genotype Aa
The frequency of heterozygotes is always greater than the combined frequency of the two homozygotes
The frequency of heterozygotes (2pq) can never exceed 0.5
The frequency of genotype aa is always equal to the frequency of allele a

solution.explanation: Genotype frequencies are p², 2pq and q² with p + q = 1. The heterozygote frequency 2pq = 2p(1 - p) is largest when p = 0.5, where it equals 0.5; for any other p it is smaller. So 2pq can never exceed 0.5. The other statements fail for some value of p: for p = 0.5, AA (0.25) is less than Aa (0.5); for p = 0.9, 2pq = 0.18 is less than p² + q² = 0.82; q² equals q only when q is 0 or 1.
steps: Counter-examples rule out the other options
solution.why_others_wrong: At p = 0.5, AA (0.25) is less than Aa (0.5); at p = 0.9, heterozygotes (0.18) are fewer than homozygotes (0.82); q² equals q only when q is 0 or 1.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 6 'Evolution', Hardy-Weinberg Principle
solution.final_answer: Option C: The frequency of heterozygotes (2pq) can never exceed 0.5

solution.explanation: NCERT: certain types of leukocytes of our body like polymorpho-nuclear leukocytes (PMNL - neutrophils), monocytes and natural killer cells (a type of lymphocyte) in the blood, as well as macrophages in tissues, can phagocytose and destroy microbes; these are the cellular barriers of innate immunity. B-lymphocytes belong to acquired immunity: they produce antibodies (humoral immune response).
steps: Cellular barriers: neutrophils (PMNL), monocytes, NK cells, macrophages
solution.why_others_wrong: Neutrophils, natural killer cells and macrophages are all named by NCERT as phagocytic cells forming the cellular barrier of innate immunity.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 7 'Human Health and Disease', Immunity

Ascariasis, filariasis, amoebiasis, ringworm, malaria, pneumonia

R: false - differentiation occurs in bone marrow and thymus

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Which option arranges the following events in the life cycle of Plasmodium in the correct order, according to NCERT?

(P) The parasites multiply within the liver cells of the human
(Q) Sporozoites enter the human body through the bite of an infected female Anopheles mosquito
(R) The parasites attack the red blood cells, which rupture and release haemozoin
(S) A female Anopheles takes up gametocytes with the blood meal, and fertilisation and development take place in its stomach
(T) Sporozoites formed in the mosquito are stored in its salivary glands

solution.explanation: NCERT: Plasmodium enters the human body as sporozoites (infectious form) through the bite of an infected female Anopheles mosquito (Q). The parasites initially multiply within the liver cells (P) and then attack the red blood cells, resulting in their rupture and release of haemozoin (R). The sexual stages (gametocytes) develop in the red blood cells; when a female Anopheles bites an infected person, these enter the mosquito, where fertilisation and development take place in the stomach (S). The parasites multiply to form sporozoites that are stored in the salivary glands (T), ready for the next bite.
steps: Q -> P (liver) -> R (RBCs) -> S (mosquito stomach) -> T (salivary glands)
solution.why_others_wrong: The parasites multiply in the liver before attacking RBCs, so R cannot precede P; sporozoites must enter before any multiplication in the human, so P cannot come first; sporozoites stored in the salivary glands are formed only after fertilisation in the mosquito, so T cannot precede S.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Biology, Ch 7 'Human Health and Disease', Common Diseases in Humans
solution.final_answer: Option D: Q -> P -> R -> S -> T
